item.title: Secretary to the Head of Division - EEAS.POL.AMERICAS.3 - Contract Agent FGII - Job No. 524345
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The South America Division is responsible for relations with ten South American countries: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela. At sub-regional level, the division follows relations with MERCOSUR and the Andean Community. Together with the Commission services and other EU institutions, we aim to shape good relations with these countries to our mutual benefit. The division ensures the supervision of, and the follow-up to existing bilateral agreements and the organisation of high-level political dialogues. It also looks at how the EU can best address possible crisis situations. WE PROPOSE The position of Secretary to the Head of the South America Division , contract agent FGII as per article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group II), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year that may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: immediately LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof. WE LOOK FOR A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. S/he will be entrusted with the following main tasks: assist the Head of Division with administrative and logistic support functions and general calendar coordination (agenda, incoming calls); the position includes regular contacts with the ten South American EU Delegations and Embassies in Brussels, and with other services of the EEAS and the Commission; provide support for the organisation of meetings: send invitations, book rooms, register visitors, request accreditation for high-level visitors and compile folders of working documents.; monitor Division deadlines and assign incoming requests (briefings, letters, inter-service consultations, etc.); organise missions of the Head of Division (mission orders, statements of expenses, book travel and accommodation, etc.); support the Head of Division with the management of human resources (e.g. publication of vacancies, selection procedures) and welcoming of newcomers; ensure document management functions: register/filter/distribute incoming mail (from Ares, Division functional mailbox, etc.); act as back-up to the other Division Assistant. Eligibility criteria Further to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in a valid function group for this post, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST in a valid function group for this post ( https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration ). In the latter case, while the registration will make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; have a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma or a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education and appropriate professional experience of three year; have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen. Selection criteria Candidates should: have good organisation and secretarial skills; have good drafting and communication skills; have good computer skills; have a good knowledge of English and Spanish (orally and in writing); be able to quickly adapt to a new working environment; be a good team-player; have knowledge of external relations, internal policies and functioning of the Union. Furthermore: knowledge of French; command of EU specialised IT tools and applications (ARES, Sysper2, e-brief, Decide, MIPS); experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in working with or within EU institutions or Delegations, in a national diplomatic service, or in a multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; will be considered as strong assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest ( see attached ). MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned. Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed. Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate. In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to CONTRACTAGENTS-HQ@eeas.europa.eu . Your request will be treated in strict confidence and no record will be kept. If a candidate with a disability is selected for a vacant post, the EEAS is committed to providing reasonable accommodation in accordance with Article 1(d)(4) of the SR. item.title: Press and Information Officer (m/f/x)
item.description: Vacancy Notice Job title: Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) LOCAL AGENT GROUP I Political, Press and Information Section We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein (Bern) works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Swiss government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Press and Information Officer (LA Group I) in the Political, Press and Information Section, under a fixed-term employment contract of two years , with the possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availability and operational considerations. The probationary period is of 3 months. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of four people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be entrusted with functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Political, Press and Information Section providing support, expertise and assistance in social media and digital communication and public relations. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: ROLE OVERVIEW As Press and Information Officer (PIO), the jobholder works under the supervision of the Head of Section and will act as the EU Delegation’s (EUDEL) spokesperson, also advising the Ambassador on all communication-related aspects. The jobholder will be the first point of contact for journalists and press. The PIO will be the key contributor to the development of the Delegation’s overall press, communication and visibility strategy. The jobholder will manage EUDEL’s digital presence, proactively propose new social media, website and video content promoting EUDEL’s activities, the EU and its values. The jobholder drives the development and implementation of EUDEL’s public diplomacy outreach, notably events organization and stakeholders’ engagement MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. PRESS, COMMUNICATION AND PUBLIC DIPLOMACY (accounting for ~85% of the jobholder’s time) PUBLIC RELATIONS & MEDIA Maintain and develop relationships with local and international journalists, media organizations, and government press agencies Prepare and disseminate press releases, press reviews, and articles for media and internet publication, as well as interviews and speeches of the Head of Delegation Develop and implement public diplomacy strategies to improve the perception of the EU in Switzerland and Liechtenstein Prepare communication materials such as speeches, briefings, and information for the media Monitor local and European media and prepare press reports Manage media requests and coordinate responses with the relevant internal stakeholders Organize press coverage during official missions and events Collaborate with EU HQ services and strategic communications task forces to ensure consistent messaging and alignment of communication strategies SOCIAL MEDIA & DIGITAL COMMUNICATION Lead the Delegation’s digital and social media strategy, managing and producing content on all relevant social media platforms and the Delegation’s website to ensure content is informative, engaging and accurate Oversee the creation and implementation of digital communication plans and social media campaigns (including cross-posting, streaming, and event coverage) Analyse social media performance and analytics, and provide / implement recommendations to improve digital communication strategies and the Delegation’s online visibility Coordinate digital campaigns with external service providers EVENT MANAGEMENT & PUBLIC OUTREACH Lead the preparation of public diplomacy events, public outreach activities, high-level visits, and site visits for the Ambassador and other EU officials Coordinate with cultural, academic, and diplomatic partners to enhance event impact and ensure successful public diplomacy campaigns Coordinate local outreach activities and organize cultural and visibility events to promote EU values and activities Organize cultural and visibility events to promote EU values and activities STRATEGIC SUPPORT & ADMINISTRATION Support in drafting reports, strategic documents, and preparing internal and external communication plans Assist with the planning and management of the Delegation's press and information budget, including procurement and contract management 2. POLICY (accounting for ~15% of the jobholder’s time) Monitoring, policy analysis and reporting: EU-CH cooperation in EU programmes, incl. Erasmus+, research, innovation, science, culture. Duties and responsibilities may be adapted according to the evolving needs of the European Union and its diplomatic representations. WORKING ENVIRONMENT WORKING CONDITIONS Employment conditions are on full time basis, with 37.5 hours per week, from Monday to Friday Atypical working hours (evening, weekend) Travel for work missions Work is performed in an office setting and involves no specific or unusual physical requirements WORKING RELATIONSHIPS The jobholder works closely with other colleagues in the Section and other members of the organization to implement communication strategies and media outreach activities. He advises the Ambassador on communication. The role also involves regular collaboration with colleagues in Headquarters and cultural, academic, and diplomatic partners, as well as external service providers for event coordination and digital campaigns. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 10,343 CHF . There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays and a retirement savings plan. Health insurance includes insurance against accident (LAA) and partial refund of LAMaL. The expected start date will be 01/03/2027. REQUIREMENTS Minimum requirements/eligibility criteria University degree in a field relevant to the position (political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or related field) Minimum 5 years of professional experience in a relevant field (media, online publishing, public relations, communication, events or similar). Professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained Excellent knowledge (C1) of German, French and English Right to residence and work in Switzerland (under the reservation of approval by the competent authorities, where applicable) Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Postgraduate degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or related field Experience in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in a multi-cultural international setting Experience working with the European Union policies and procedures SKILLS Ability to translate complicated policy issues into traditional and social media compatible language Ability to develop communication strategies and plans Good network within Swiss media Very good understanding of local and European cultural interaction Good knowledge of the EU Institutions, history and priorities, and of EU-Switzerland relations Very good knowledge of digital media and communication techniques Very good knowledge of graphic and layout editing and design tools Very good knowledge of Web publication tools Excellent writing skills and ability to produce concise and clear notes Communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing BEHAVIORAL ATTRIBUTES Capacity to multitask and to work under time pressure Ability to work proactively and take appropriate actions, without being prompted by others Ability to adapt quickly and flexibly to new requests Ability to foster connections and maintain good professional relationships with external stakeholders Ability to work in a multicultural team, showing good interpersonal skills Capacity to focus on priorities, to show initiative and to organize own workload to respect deadlines Comfortable speaking to a large audience to lead or introduce public events Service-oriented mindset, with a professional attitude and appearance Eager to learn and develop new knowledge and competences High degree of integrity, confidentiality and responsibility How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter , signed a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers’ names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en to the following email address: eeasjobs-078@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: Ref: 157570 – Press and Information Officer no later than 18/09/2026 at 24:00 (CET). Applications can be submitted in English or French. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application. item.title: VACANCY: Accounts Clerk
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the United Republic of Tanzania and to the East African Community, Dar es Salaam works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Tanzania government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Local Agent Job Profile of Accounts Clerk, Group III in the Delegation’s Administration Section, under a fixed-term employment contract of 2 years (9 months’ probation period), with a possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availability and operational considerations. The team consists of 13 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed to functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Administration Section, providing support in the control and maintenance of accounts and in the processing of financial transactions, in accordance with existing rules and regulations, typically provides support in the maintenance of specific accounts, monitoring expenditure, calculation and compilation of financial data and in the preparation of routine reports and annual budget estimates. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: ACCOUNTS MANAGEMENT Act as initiating agent in the Delegation’s financial management system: reception and verification of incoming invoices and internal requests for payment, check against related documentation (contracts, purchase orders, order forms, internal documents, etc.) Register commercial invoices, internal documents or credit notes in the financial system SUMMA and ensure payment within the deadline, in accordance with the EU Financial Regulation Execute payments in local bank accounts and follow up outstanding and non-executed bank transactions Maintain the database and ensure the approval of contractors in the financial system (Legal Entities, Bank Account, Financial Identification of contractors and members of staff) Encode the requests, commitments and de-commitments in the budget forecast software, in the accounting system and in the mission management software Manage "petty" cash accounts BUDGET MONITORING AND REPORTING Follow up, adjust and verify the execution of the authorised budget, in compliance with the financial regulations Assisting in the preparation and follow up of annual and interim administrative budget Prepare the closure / reconciliation / monthly reporting Prepare files for "ex-post control" requests ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT Calculate mission costs estimates, assist in verification of mission claims and representation expenses, and liquidate the relating expenses Assist with procurement procedures and contracts management: prepare purchase orders and order forms, upload contracts in the dedicated platform, follow up with the contracts’ consumption Assist in the preparation of the monthly payroll for local agents (including the calculation of overtime, salary arrears, etc.) and in the management of rights and obligations of expatriate staff (e.g., temporary accommodation, additional costs etc.) Other administrative duties as assigned by HoA and or HoD The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 3,573,768 TZS. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 16 October 2026. Working Conditions 37.5 working hours per week Occasional overtime outside of typical working hours (evening, weekend) Occasional travel for work missions Work is performed in an office setting and involves no specific or unusual physical requirements Working Relationships Interacts with staff at different levels within the Delegation to provide information and clarifications and to follow-up on anomalies and verify input. Maintains contacts within the Delegation and with other internal and external stakeholders, as requested by the management. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Skills Good command (min. CEFR B1 level) of English Basic knowledge of the EU Financial Regulation and the relevant financial rules and accounting policies Knowledge of corporate financial systems used for processing financial, budgeting and accounting records Ability to identify data discrepancies and operational problems Ability to use and interpret quantitative information Attention to detail and focused on accuracy of information Communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing Proficient use of standard office information technology tools and systems and ability to learn new corporate applications Behavioral Attributes Ability to work in a multicultural team, showing good interpersonal skills and respect for diversity Ability to adapt quickly and flexibly to new requests and evolving priorities Capacity to focus on priorities, to show initiative and to organize own workload in order to respect deadlines, within agreed objectives and instructions and informing the management when issues arise Service-oriented mindset Eager to learn and develop new knowledge and competences High degree of integrity, confidentiality and sense of responsibility, with a strong sense of discretion, neutrality and loyalty to the EU Eligibility criteria (minimum requirements) Post-secondary degree in accounting, audit, finance or equivalent 3 years of relevant professional experience after the degree (accounting, audit, finance, etc.) Good command of English (min. CEFR B1 level) Right to residence and work in the country Medical fitness to carry out the required duties Selection criteria (assets) Experience working in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in an international organization Experience working with the European Union tools, policies and procedures Master’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or similar Knowledge of other EU languages (French, Spanish, German or Italian) The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing and interviews. At least 2 best candidates will be invited to the final. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check, and background check. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the following functional mailbox: delegation-tanzania-hr-recruitment@eeas.europa.eu . (Applications should not be sent to this mailbox; please use the address provided in the ‘How to Apply’ section above) . Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality, preventing discrimination on any grounds and ensuring a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation at the following mailbox: delegation-tanzania-hr-recruitment@eeas.europa.eu . in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations. item.title: The European Union Delegation to Argentina is looking for: Secretary in the Politics, Press and Information Section
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Argentina works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Argentinian government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Secretary (Local Agent Group 3) in the Delegation’s Politics, Press and Information Section. The team consists of 5 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. As a Secretary, the jobholder is responsible for performing a variety of administrative and secretarial support services contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the Section. The jobholder ensures the flow and management of information by setting priorities and organizing the day-to-day routine. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES SECRETARIAL SUPPORT Manage the correspondence, communication, workflows, organisation of meetings and ensure adequate follow-up. Brings to the management and other relevant colleagues attention complex, sensitive or priority issues and provides information and basic administrative guidance to other colleagues Arrange appointments and maintain the management and team calendar, receive visitors, place and screen telephone calls, manage functional mailboxes, direct queries to the appropriate colleagues Act as a contact point for routine administrative questions within the section and support the handling and distribution of incoming and outgoing correspondence in line with the applicable procedures Organise meetings (including, where relevant, high-level meetings), finalise agendas and invitations, ensure the production and distribution of documentation, take notes and prepare minutes of meetings, and follow up on required actions Coordinate mission arrangements (travel and hotel arrangements, appointments, expense management and protocol issues) for the management and, where required, other colleagues Proofread documents and edit texts for accuracy, grammar, punctuation and style, as well as for adherence to established standards for format Assist with data encoding in corporate IT systems Support in the protocol area during official visits Back-up for the Assistant Head of Delegation ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT Organise and facilitate the administrative work of the office, including contributing to the improvement of internal procedures and tracking systems for correspondence and documents. Verify that work is done in accordance with corporate standards and deadlines. Monitor work progress and brings cases of priority issues and matters of concern to the attention of the management and other colleagues Prepare briefing materials for the management and other colleagues, and draft responses to non-routine written enquiries, based on input provided by other relevant colleagues Follow up on the preparation by staff of reports, correspondence, briefing notes and other documents, by monitoring deadlines and ensuring proper transmission and filing. Perform general administrative tasks (e.g. checking leave and attendance records, arrangements for meetings and other events, basic budget follow-up, Management of the Head of Section’s representation expenses) and coordinate with other Sections to ensure smooth running and expedition of work within the Section Orients new colleagues to relevant administrative procedures, tools and practices Other tasks in compliance with the instructions of the hierarchy WORKING ENVIRONMENT WORKING CONDITIONS 37.5 working hours per week Occasional overtime outside of typical working hours (evening, weekend) Occasional travel for work missions Work is performed in an office setting and involves no specific or unusual physical requirements WORKING RELATIONSHIPS Plays a key role in the overall provision of administrative and secretarial support services to the management and other staff at different levels, including providing training and guidance and advising the management on administrative issues within their area of responsibility. Maintains an extensive range of contacts both within the Delegation as a whole and with other internal and external stakeholders. The place of work will be in the offices of the Delegation in Buenos Aires – Address: Carlos M. DELLA PAOLERA 261 Piso 15, C1001ADA with a team of 28 staff members. The employment contract will be indefinite. The position will be hired in Group 3, working 37.5 hours per week under a flexible working hours system with a mandatory presence between 9am and 12pm and between 2pm and 4pm and with a totally competitive remuneration based on a fixed salary grid that is reviewed annually. The expected start date is 01/10/2026. REQUIREMENTS SKILLS Very good command of English (min. CEFR C1 level) Good knowledge of the relevant corporate procedures and guidelines Ability to coordinate, monitor and follow-up tasks and workflows, including the respect of deadlines Proficient use of communication and office equipment Ability to analyse and structure information efficiently Excellent drafting skills and ability to produce concise and clear notes Communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing Proficient use of standard office information technology tools and systems and ability to learn new corporate applications BEHAVIOURAL ATTRIBUTES Ability to work in a multicultural team, showing good interpersonal skills and respect for diversity Ability to adapt quickly and flexibly to new requests and evolving priorities Capacity to focus on priorities, to show initiative and to organise own workload in order to respect deadlines, within agreed objectives and instructions and informing the management when issues arise Service-oriented mindset Eager to learn and develop new knowledge and competences High degree of integrity, confidentiality and sense of responsibility, with a strong sense of discretion, neutrality and loyalty to the EU ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA (MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS) 2 years of relevant professional experience (secretary, personal assistant, office manager, administrative assistant, etc.) if holding a post-secondary degree OR 5 years of relevant professional experience (secretary, personal assistant, office manager, administrative assistant, etc.) if holding a secondary degree Post-secondary degree (ISCED level 4) OR secondary degree (ISCED level 3) Fluency written and spoken in Spanish (Level C2); Very good command of English (min. CEFR C1 level) Right to residence and work in the country Medical fitness to carry out the required duties Certificate of good conduct SELECTION CRITERIA (ASSETS) Experience working in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in an international organisation Experience working with the European Union tools, policies and procedures Post-secondary degree in secretarial studies, office management, business administration or similar (ISCED level 4) Short-cycle tertiary degree in secretarial studies, office management, business administration or similar (ISCED level 5) Language certification in French (min. CEFR B2 level) How to apply: Please submit your application, consisting of a cover letter and Europass format CV ( https://europass.europa.eu/en ) to email eeasjobs-205@eeas.europa.eu (Reference: Secretary 2026/001) no later than 04/09/2026, 13 hs. (Argentina time) . Only complete applications received on time to this email will be considered. The successful candidate will be subject to medical and background checks. The process: After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. The shortlisting of candidates will be based on the assessment of information provided in the cover letter and the CV. Between three and six best candidates will be invited to the final Selection stage, composed of a practical test and an interview. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, it is prohibited to contact the members of the Selection Committee. Questions and comments may only be addressed to the Delegation’s Administration.

item.title: Policy Officer (Digital Transformation) in the Trade Section - 2 Year Contract Subject to Renewal
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the United States of America, Washington DC is looking for: Policy Officer (Digital Transformation) in the Trade Section - 2 Year Contract Subject to Renewal We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the United States of America in Washington, DC works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the U.S. government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer We offer an interesting, challenging and very dynamic position of a Digital Transformation Policy Officer (Local Agent Group I) in the Trade Section. The section, comprising 14 people in total, is managed by the Head of the Trade and Agriculture section. One diplomat and two local agents are in charge of covering digital and technology policy. In this position, you would report to the Head of Section on tasks related to digital transformation, namely: Monitoring and reporting on the United States digital transformation policy developments, including but not limited to Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, online platform governance. Contributing to requests for briefings, speeches and notes coming from the Ambassador and Deputy Chief of Mission, as well as headquarters. Advising and supporting headquarters in defining the overall strategic approach to EU-US digital cooperation. Supporting the preparations of visits of the European Commission Executive Vice-President, other Commissioners, and high-level officials from EU Institutions. Liaising with stakeholders in the U.S. Congress, industry, civil society, think tanks and academia, the diplomatic missions of EU Member States in the US, and actors beyond the D.C. area, such as States lawmakers, involved in artificial intelligence, emerging tech and digital policies. Assisting in the preparation of bilateral EU-U.S. policy dialogues and following up on the main conclusions linked to the promotion of EU policy frameworks, technologies, standards, industrial practices. Assisting in the preparation of regular meetings of Member States Counsellors in charge of digital and tech. Promoting the EU Digital Agenda objectives and identifying opportunities for the development of strategic cooperation with the US in digital matters; including visits to Brussels and relevant Member States. Support to internal and external missions, ad hoc representations of the EU in relevant meetings or conferences. Organising and giving presentations of EU digital policies and initiatives at conferences, seminars and workshops. Supporting the European Commission’s DG CNECT, in particular the EU AI Office, in their supervisory work. Closely coordinating within the EU Delegation, and the Delegation’s Office in San Francisco, contributing to and leading joint reporting inter alia on issues of AI policy. The post involves occasional atypical working hours. In return, you will work in a section with a great team spirit and in an environment, which will allow you to develop professionally and deepen your understanding of the functioning of the European Union. There is a competitive benefits package as follows: The basic salary range (excluding overtime) is not negotiable but determined by proof of relevant and verified employment experience, starting from $134K (3 years’ experience), $137K (6 years’ experience), $144K (10 years’ experience) etc. 24 personal leave days per year 13 to 14 Public Holidays per year Flexible working hours Health, dental and vision insurance Short term disability insurance Generous employer 401k contribution This is a 2 Year Contract subject to renewal. There may be 2 renewals up to a maximum 7 years of successive fixed-term contracts. An indefinite contract may be offered after 7 years. The anticipated start date is 1 November/1 December 2026. Eligibility requirements Minimum of a Bachelor’s/University Degree in social sciences (international relations or digital economy matters) or a similarly related field. A Master’s degree is an advantage; Minimum of 3 year’s proven experience in policy monitoring, evaluation and briefing skills. We look for We look for a committed and energetic colleague with strong experience and proven track record as a Policy Adviser (minimum 3 years). You should have: Strong writing and analytical skills, and the ability to write clearly and concisely; Proven capacity to focus on priorities, to multi-task and to organise work to deliver on time in a structured manner, often within tight deadlines; Outstanding capacity to work and feel at ease in a diverse team; high flexibility and capacity to work under pressure, efficiency and resourcefulness; Solid knowledge and experience of EU's digital policies and the US digital transformation ecosystem and polices; Excellent proficiency of English (written and spoken); a command of at least one other European language is considered an advantage; Excellent computer skills (and knowledge of commonly used programs such as Microsoft office suite). See the full listing at Indeed .

item.title: Market assessment and expression of interest - EU4Rivers
item.description: Market assessment and expression of interest - EU4Rivers Text The European Union (EU) has delegated the Austrian Development Agency (ADA) to implement the project “EU for Water” - Component 1& 2 (“ EU4Rivers ”). The overall objective is to maintain or improve Albania's water bodies and marine quality status. The specific objective is to increase Albania’s approximation with the EU water acquis. Within the specific objective, the following outputs are foreseen: Output 1: The overarching IWM legal and institutional framework is substantially enhanced in line with the requirements of the EU acquis (Water Framework Directive/WFD and other water-related directives). Output 2: The Implementation of River Basins Management is increased in all river basins in line with the requirements of the WFDs Output 3: Water monitoring, reporting and enforcement are sustainably enhanced in line with water-related EU Directives' requirements. Output 4: The strategic and institutional framework for the implementation of the MSFD is established. To address the needs of Albanian institutions and public in line with the above mentioned outputs, EU4Rivers provides its support through professional technical expertise and equipment/supply. In that context, the project is looking for expression of Interests (EoI) in different areas from qualified and experienced experts/consultancies (legal entities) that might be invited to submit offers. Interested candidates who have been engaged previously with ADA and/or have expressed their EoI in the past are requested to submit their updated CV accordingly. At this first stage, candidates who meet the requirements as specified in the following areas are invited to submit their EoI: AREA OF EXPERTISE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE EXPERT LEGAL / ENVIRONMENTAL EXPERT Experts with background in Law, Environmental Management or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in water sector, in drafting and implementing transboundary agreements and supporting transboundary mechanisms are eligible/invited to apply. GIS/ Cartography expert Experts with background in GIS/Cartography, Geoinformatics, Environmental Engineering or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in GIS data management, spatial analysis and preparation of thematic maps relevant to water status assessment are eligible/invited to apply. Hydrologist / Climate Change and Drought Risk Assessment Expert Experts with background in Hydrology, Water Resources Engineering Environmental Management or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in hydrology and water-resources assessment, including but not limited to experience in climate-change impact assessment, drought analysis or climate-resilient water management are eligible/invited to apply. Hydrogeologist / Groundwater Status Assessment Expert Experts with background in Hydrogeology, Geology or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in hydrogeology or groundwater management, groundwater monitoring, status assessment or implementation of EU water legislation are eligible/invited to apply. Environmental / Surface water Status Assessment Expert Experts with background in Hydrology, Environmental Management or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in water or environmental assessment, including surface-water monitoring, and ecological and/or chemical status assessment under the EU Water Framework Directive are eligible/invited to apply. Environmental economist Experts with background in Environmental Economy, Public finance Management or similar field, with at least 7 years of professional experience in economic/financial analysis, cost estimation, or public investment planning, of which a minimum of 5 years of experience in investment cost estimation and economic assessment for environmental/infrastructure programmes are eligible/invited to apply. The respective EOI must be sent to eu4rivers@ada.gv.at by 21September 2026 indicating “ Area: __/EU4rivers ” in the subject and including a CV in English language using the standard EU format , a cover letter and up-to-date extract from the Register of Companies or equivalent certificate issued by a court or administrative authority. The submitted documents (CV and other documents) are foreseen to be used for later procurement procedures and interested experts might be invited. ADA will retain the personal data until the finalization of the EU4Rivers project, which is currently planned for 30.09.2028. For further details, please refer to our Privacy Notice: www.entwicklung.at/en/media-centre/privacy-notice .

item.title: VACANCY NOTICE: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Ukraine in Kyiv works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Ukrainian government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of an Administrative Assistant (Local Agent Job Profile of Administrative Assistant, Group II) in the Delegation’s Administration Section to assist the EU Delegation Regional Security Team, under a fixed-term employment contract of 3 years, with a possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availabilities and operational considerations. For internal candidates currently holding an indefinite-term employment contract, any contractual arrangement following selection will be determined in accordance with applicable local labour law and institutional policies. The team consists of 25 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Administration Section or his/her substitute, providing support, expertise and assistance to the EU Delegation Regional Security Team with non-classified administrative tasks. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: Security Information Analysis Systematically collecting non-classified information related to the evolution of security threats across Ukraine and neighbouring countries (security events and incidents), as well as any other elements that may affect the security interests of the EU Delegation; Maintaining non-classified incident logs and non-classified security databases related to security events and incidents; Analysing and processing non-classified security events and incidents in order to provide the Regional Security Team with an up-to-date security situational picture, including through non-classified verbal briefings, written reports, and presentations. Security Operations Assisting the Regional Security Team with non-classified administrative aspects related to the implementation of the EEAS and EU Delegation’s standard operating procedures and contingency plans; Accompanying, when required by the Regional Security Team, mission personnel during field missions in the country. Liaison and Coordination Assisting the Regional Security Team with non-classified administrative aspects related to liaison and coordination with host nation security actors (e.g., military, law enforcement, and intelligence services), as well as national, local, and provincial authorities, including attending non-classified virtual and in-person meetings when required. Compliance Assisting the Regional Security Team with non-classified administrative aspects related to the Framework Contract for Security Services of the EU Delegation Maintaining, under the supervision of the Regional Security Team, the warden system and ensuring that information related to EUDEL local staff is kept up to date. Training and Awareness The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 2950 USD currency. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be November 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Higher level qualifications and/or higher level vocational studies; Valid driver’s license: category B Minimum of 6 years of relevant experience in: Security management (security operation supervisor) Risk analysis or intelligence Diplomatic or international organization security environment . The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Working knowledge (C1) of written and spoken English; Working knowledge (C1) of written and spoken Ukrainian; Knowledge of IT tools: MS Word, Excel, Access, Power Point, digital mapping and GIS system; Right to residence and work in Ukraine; Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) University degree or equivalent; Knowledge of VHF and UHF radio operation; Knowledge of CCTV environment; Experience in high-risk or conflict-affected environments is highly desirable; Knowledge of Russian. Personal skills Analytical thinking and sound judgment; Crisis response capability; Strong reporting skills; Ability to work under pressure; Discretion and confidentiality; Effective liaison and coordination skills. Specific physical requirements Position based in Kyiv with frequent travel within Ukraine; Exposure to high-risk and dynamic security conditions; May require availability outside normal working hours. How to apply The applicant must apply by sending: a cover letter in English, signed a Curriculum Vitæ in English (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en all documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-210@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “Ref: 521660 – JOB TITLE: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT“ no later than 15/09/2026. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. At least 3 best candidates will be invited to the final Selection phase. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. item.title: The European Union Delegation to the Republic of Colombia, in Bogotá is looking for: Driver in the Administration section.
item.description: Vacancy Notice Job title: Driver LOCAL AGENT GROUP V Ref: 355421 - Administration Section 01 September 2026 We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Republic of Colombia, in Bogotá works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Colombian government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Driver (Local Agent Job Profile of Driver, Group V) in the Delegation’s Administration Section. Under a fixed-term employment contract of two years, with the possibility of renewal for an additional two years under reserve of budgetary availabilities and operational considerations. After this period, in accordance with the new labour law, the contract would then become indefinite (if confirmed). For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of 13 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Administration Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in field of driving and service. Following main tasks and duties are currently required Act as a driver for the Head of Delegation and other members of staff of the Delegation and their guests to official meetings and other places related to work, or in mission within Colombia, during the working day and after hours as necessary. Take responsibility for collecting and delivering mail to the post office or Ministries and other governmental and non-governmental agencies, and other official documents to and from their relevant destination in Bogotá. To keep track and record of vehicle daily activity in the provided vehicle logbooks. Ensure that the vehicle's mandatory legal documents (insurance, etc.) are in order and valid and kept in the vehicle. Ensure that the vehicle is clean and in good driving condition before using it (carry out routine checks such as tire pressure, lights, fluids, etc.). Ensure that the vehicle is fuelled, cleaned and washed when needed. Inform the office manager when the vehicle needs mechanical revision or spare parts and keep track of the maintenance records in the vehicles’ files. Request quotes for maintenance work in advance for authorization, coordinate maintenance appointments with authorized repair garages and verify the proper performance of the authorized works. Assists in operational protocol matters when accompanying high-level visits. Assists the Administration section with other operational tasks as required. item.title: EEAS Call for Expression of Interest for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) as Secretary (AST/SC2) POL.EURCA.EAST.1 - Ukraine Division
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The Ukraine Division is responsible for policy definition and strategic planning for EU’s bilateral relations with Ukraine and for providing support and advice to the HRVP, to EEAS Management, to Commission management and the President of the European Council, on all aspects of EU-Ukraine relations. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one SECRETARY (AST/SC2) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Open/register/filter incoming mail (Ares) and assign mail appropriately; Open mail in Division functional mailbox and reply/assign as necessary; Ensure the follow-up of briefing requests and the respect of deadlines; Organise missions (prepare mission orders and statements of expenses in MIPS, book travel and accommodation, etc.); Answer and filter telephone calls; Keep agenda, organise and co-ordinate meetings and share information as needed with Division members; Provide logistical support for the organisation of meetings / briefings: reserve rooms, register visitors, request accreditation for high-level visitors and compile folders of working documents; Compose routine correspondence; Carry out various tasks such as diary keeping, filing and ordering office supplies; Back-up to the Administrative Assistant to the Head of Division. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST/SC2. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 3 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties; OR Relevant professional training followed by at least 3 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: Have proven experience in the administrative support field; Have a good sense of initiative, prioritisation and team work; Have sound computer skills (MS Office) and experience in using workflow based IT applications; Have an excellent working command of English and knowledge of French. Furthermore: Good knowledge of standard administrative IT applications used in the EEAS or in the European Commission (ARES, MIPS, Sysper2, EU-Learn, e-Brief); Knowledge of EEAS/Commission working procedures; Experience in an Embassy/EU Delegation/EU CSDP mission; Knowledge of other languages; would be considered as strong assets. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox pol-eurca-east-1@eeas.europa.eu copying AST-SC-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: "EoI-HQ (AST/SC)-TA2b-AST/SC2-POL.EURCA.EAST.1 job 400478" Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 18/09/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: "EoI-HQ (AST/SC)-TA2b-AST/SC2- POL.EURCA.EAST.1 job 400478" ) : AST-SC-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu 2. Pre-selection The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter. 3. Selection The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs. Depending on the outcome of future appointment procedure(s) under Article 29 of the SR for a similar profile , EEAS services may, in case no suitable candidates are found among EU officials, have other job opportunities that would involve the recruitment of the Temporary Agents under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. If any, candidates in the above-mentioned reserve list may be contacted by other EEAS services for potential recruitment. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion . The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to EEAS-HQ-APPLICATIONS-AST@eeas.europa.eu . Your request will be treated in strict confidence and no record will be kept. If a candidate with a disability is selected for a vacant post, the EEAS is committed to providing reason

item.title: Funded traineeship for young graduates at the EU Delegation to Costa Rica
item.description: Are you a young graduate interested in international relations? Are you curious to learn more about work of a diplomatic mission and how the EU Delegation represents EU interests and values in Costa Rica? We offer: A traineeshipof up to 6 months in 2026 within the Political, Press and Information Section (PPI Section of the EU Delegation,. The tentative start date is November 2026. Under the supervision and mentoring of a Trainee’s supervisor, this Funded traineeship will provide a solid and meaningful learning content, notably by the prior identification of the specific skills to be acquired in relation with the studies of the candidates. Main tasks : Expand awareness of EU external action in its multiple dimensions, with focus on human rights and democracy, security and justice Improve knowledge of the strategic priorities of EU relations with Latin America and the Caribbean and concretely with Costa Rica Build practical knowledge of the functioning of an EU Delegation by contributing to its activities in terms of political reporting and coordination with MS, as well as public diplomacy and communication Initiation in negotiation and reporting techniques in a multicultural and multilinguistic environment Develop communication skills, both oral and written, by contributing to press statements, social media, organisation of events, speech writing Building hard skills in the design and creation of audio-visual content to assist in the creation of political communication campaigns in digital areas such as social networks Develop knowledge in strategic plans for political communication, by analyzing international affairs, stakeholder and target audience mapping, creating narratives, and others Protocol and diplomatic etiquette Contribute to the daily monitoring of press and information in Costa Rica; Assist in the organisation of outreach and visibility events for both PPI and Cooperation Sections; Support the implementation of cultural activities and the coordination with EU Member States in the field; Contributing to the Delegation's weekly press review. We look for: Qualifications or special requirements : Young graduates with less than one year of professional experience, Citizens of the host country, nationals from the EU Member States or States which have signed an accession agreement with EU Young graduates with at least a Bachelor Diploma (or equivalent) Maximum one year of professional experience No previous experience of more than six weeks in the EU institutions How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address DELEGATION-COSTA-RICA-TRAINEESHIP@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents: A detailed standard Europass curriculum vitae ( CV ) https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/ (CVs in other format will not be considered) a cover letter describing why you want to participate in a EU traineeship and an application form: Application form for funded traineeships 2026.docx Please mention in the subject of your e-mail : Funded Traineeship - PPI - Section Important information to read before applying Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Citizens from EU Member states: must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation; must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation.

Encoding, processing and follow up of transactions in the corporate IT systems. Financial planning, budgeting, reporting, audits, and verification on project / contracts / programs. Preparation and follow-up of audit and control plans for programs and projects, including on-the-spot checks and verification missions. Preparation and verification of tender dossiers and documents for calls for proposals. Participation in evaluation committees. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from ZAR78,046.00. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 01/12/2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) University Degree in Accounting / Finance / Project management (min. 4 years) or equivalent. Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in financial management of development projects / programmes. Professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Working knowledge (B2) of English Right to residence and work in South Africa. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Master’s degree in accounting / finance / Project management Certification: Fraud Prevention / Financial Investigation / Development cooperation Professional experience in diplomatic mission, international financial institution or international development agency French and / or Sesotho language, OPSYS, CRIS, ABAC, SUMMA Knowledge/experience of EU policies, in the Kingdom of Lesotho How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter , signed a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employer’s names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass template available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en all documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-221@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email subject: “Ref: 514366 – Budget Officer” no later than 18:00 hours (UTC+02:00) 18/09/2026. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfills all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must tick all the relevant checkboxes in the application document. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. At least the 3 best candidates will be invited to the final interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check and possible background check. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response.
