item.title: Funded traineeships for young graduates at the EU Delegation to the United States
item.description: Are you a young graduate interested in international relations? Are you curious to learn more about work of a diplomatic mission and how the EU Delegation represents EU interests and values in United States of America? We offer: Traineeships of up to 6 months within the following sections of the EU Delegation to the United States, subject to availability of the budget. The tentative start date is November 2026. Traineeship in the Administration Section (ADMIN): The Administration section provides support services to the Delegation staff, building, and residences. It encompasses Human Resources, Accounting & Finance, Infrastructure, and Information Technology. It liaises with authorities in Europe and the United States on protocol and administrative matters related to EU officials. As a trainee in the Admin section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Support the logistical coordination and organization of meetings, events, workshops, and official visits, including escorting visitors to the Delegation. Receive, organize, and maintain office stationery, supplies, and other materials. Maintain accurate records of suppliers, orders, deliveries, and expenditures. Provide general administrative and clerical support to the Section, including filing, correspondence, scheduling, and document management. Attend internal and external meetings and prepare minutes, action points, and follow-up records. Assist with maintaining organized records and ensuring that administrative activities are completed efficiently and on time. Assist with market surveys Traineeship in the Global Issues and Innovation section (GIN): The Global Issues and Innovation section monitors and analyses U.S. political, economic, and regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety (which includes plant and animal health and animal welfare), public health, and consumer protection. As a trainee in the Global Issues and Innovation section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Researching U.S. regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, climate, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety, public health, and consumer protection. Attending U.S. Congressional hearings and other public events related to section policy areas and writing summaries for the section. Support the preparation of the Delegation’s outreach activities within the GIN section areas. Preparing minutes of section meetings. Traineeship in the Head of Delegation section (HOD): The Head of Delegation Section (HOD) supports the work of both the Ambassador and Deputy Ambassador in promoting positive relations with the United States. The HOD team coordinates with all Sections across the Delegation to establish priorities for the Ambassador’s agenda, ensure briefing for all scheduled meetings and engagements, coordinate a high number of social and diplomatic functions at the EU residence (dinners, lunches, receptions and events), and plan several State Outreach visits per year to build relationships at the State level with elected officials, business leaders and civil society. The HOD team also works with the wider Delegation to ensure the Ambassador’s participation in all high-level visits from Headquarters, and prepares the monthly coordination meetings of EU Ambassadors and Deputy Ambassadors as well as a monthly briefing call with EU Consuls General serving as EU Local Chairs around the US. The HOD intern will primarily be tasked to assist on State Outreach planning and events hosted by the Ambassador at the official EU Residence. As a trainee in the HOD section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: State Outreach: Conducting preliminary research to identify suitable meetings/events/partner in the destination State Assisting with pre-trip planning calls with contacts in the destination State Briefing assembly Post-trip follow-up correspondence Support to Social Secretary for Events at EU Residence Ad Hoc special projects at request of Ambassador Traineeship in the Political section (POL): The Political Section follows all aspects of the transatlantic agenda and closely monitors the work of Congress and the U.S. Administration on foreign, security, and defence policy, counterterrorism and home affairs, and human rights, as well as U.S. domestic policy and U.S. elections. The section maintains regular contact with a broad range of Washington-based NGOs, think tanks, and civil society organizations. As a trainee in the Political section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Attending virtual U.S. Congressional hearings and writing summaries. Attending think tank events and writing summaries of topics covered. Researching and writing reports on foreign policy, security, and development cooperation issues for the section. Contributing to briefings on issues related to the section’s priorities. Assisting with the organization of outreach events and activities related to political, security and development issues. Traineeship in the Press and Public Diplomacy section (PPD): The Press and Public Diplomacy section aims to highlight the work of the EU to various audiences in the U.S. As a horizontal section, PPD is the key coordinator of all the Delegation’s public outreach activities. The section is also responsible for the Delegation’s media relations and communications strategy. In addition, the section manages people-to-people initiatives and is in charge of the EU’s cultural diplomacy in the U.S. As a trainee in the Press and Public Diplomacy section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Assisting with the organization of public diplomacy events. Assisting with media monitoring and analysis and support for press events. Supporting the section with social media communication and digital content creation (website and social media). Monitoring events organized by think tanks and other organizations for reporting purposes. Providing research assistance as needed in areas related to the section's priorities. Preparing minutes of meetings and assisting with drafting briefings. Answering general information requests. Qualifications or special requirements : Must have at least a Bachelor's Diploma and background in relevant disciplines (International Affairs, European Affairs, Political Science, Law, Communications, Environment, Health, Science, Economics and other related policy areas). Excellent command of the English language. Be available full time, Monday through Friday. How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address delegation-usa-internships@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents: Please mention in the subject of your e-mail : Funded Traineeship - ADMIN, GIN, HOD, POL, or PPD (you may only apply to 1 traineeship per delegation, however based on your profile, the delegation could offer you a traineeship in another section). Important information to read before applying Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Citizens from EU Member states: must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation; must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation.

item.title: Short Deadline: 19 national staff positions with EUPM Armenia
item.description: The European Union Partnership Mission in Armenia (EUPM) is a civilian mission dedicated to strengthening Armenia’s resilience and its capacity to address foreign information manipulation and interference, cyber-threats, as well as illicit financial flows. The Mission supports this objective through the provision of strategic guidance, operational-level advice, and capacity building assistance to relevant security sector institutions. Working in line with a whole of government approach and in close coordination with international partners and like-minded actors, the Mission contributes to enhancing Armenia’s democratic resilience, crisis management capabilities, and institutional preparedness. EUPM Armenia offers nineteen (19) positions across a diverse team of professionals specialising in executive coordination, political affairs and communications, project management, interpretation, administration, finance, logistics, procurement, information systems, security, transportation, and human resources to support the effective implementation of its mandate in Armenia. We offer a working opportunity in an international environment with a professional atmosphere. It is full-time work, in a multicultural environment. Working hours: 40 hours/week Place of employment: Yerevan, Armenia Duration: One-year fixed-term contract, including a three-month probationary period, with the possibility of contract renewal subject to budget approval and the future mandate of the Mission. Salary Group: The applicable salary group is indicated in the job description. Salary will be determined based on qualifications and experience within the relevant salary range : Group 1: 1,403,627 - 3,011,455 AMD/month Group 2: 964,404 – 1,765,743 AMD/month Group 3: 642.051 – 1,297,906 AMD/month Availability : As soon as possible Deadline for applications : 24:00, 13 September 2026 For detailed Job Descriptions, please read further on the Post Title listed in the table below. Job titles / Vacancy Notice: See detailed profiles here . Essential Requirements: Medically fit to perform the required duties; Enjoys civil rights and permits for employment under local law; Proficiency in English and Armenian both oral and written, Russian when applicable. Level of education as indicated in the respective Job Description; After having fulfilled the education requirements, number of years of relevant professional experience, as indicated in the respective Job Description, in performing duties relevant to the job description; Any other requirements as specified in the Job Description. The selection procedure After the deadline for applications, the applications will be reviewed by the Selection Panel, which will establish a shortlist of candidates considered to be the most suitable for the post on the basis of a preliminary assessment of the information provided in the Application Forms. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an assessment phase, which will include an interview and, if required, additional tests. During this phase, the Selection Panel will assess the suitability of the candidates for the post. Applicants who are not shortlisted will be informed once the selection procedure has been completed and the position has been filled. For more information relating to the recruitment and selection process, please contact job@eupm-armenia.eu

item.description: We offer : A traineeship of up to 6 months in the Political, Press and Information section of the EU Delegation to Singapore, starting in November 2026. item.title: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT (PROTOCOL)
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, in Amman, works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the 27 government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Administrative Assistant (Protocol) (Local Agent Job Profile of Administrative Assistant, Group II) in the Delegation’s Common Administration Section, under a fixed-term employment contract of 2 years, with a possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availabilities and operational considerations. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of 29 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Common Administration Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in the Administration field. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: Liaison between the delegation and the national authorities (mainly the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates) for all matters related to protocol matters; Draft of all correspondence relating to registration and other formalities for expatriate staff and dependents; follow-up with all relevant administrations (customs, Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of Labour, etc.); Organisation of VIP visits in close cooperation with national authorities, including, if necessary, the Royal Court; Maintenance of section administrative records (protocol procedures); classification, filing and recording of correspondence and documents; Advice on the procedures to be implemented to solve in a correct and fast way the particular files; External stakeholder relations regarding events and public affairs; Relations with the building landlord representatives; Drivers and cars fleet coordinator. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 1,940.00 Jordanian Dinars. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be in November 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or any related field; Minimum of 3 years of professional experience, including 2 years of relevant experience as a Protocol Officer. The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained; Working knowledge - written and spoken - of English (B2) and Arabic (C1); Right to residence and work in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan; Excellent knowledge of computer applications: Excel, Word, scheduling and communication; Energetic person, able to handle several strands of work in parallel in a high-pressure; environment. The ability to work with others is vital; Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Good communication skills; Experience and ability to work in a multicultural environment; Previous professional experience working in an Embassy or international organization as aa Protocol Officer; Knowledge of the customs system is an asset. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. Best candidates will be invited to the final placement test, and an interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. item.title: VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT FOR THE POST OF PROGRAMME ASSOCIATE (WASH, Shelter and Settlements))
item.description: DG ECHO is recruiting one National Staff to be based in Nairobi (Kenya) as a Programme Associate (WASH, Shelter & Settlements) , for its Nairobi Regional Office. REF. ECHO/PA/NRO The European Commission’s Directorate General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO) funds relief operations for victims of natural disasters and conflicts outside the European Union. DG ECHO works with about 200 operational partners, including United Nations agencies, the Red Cross/Crescent movement, and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Aid is channelled impartially, straight to victims, regardless of their race, ethnic group, religion, gender, age, nationality, or political affiliation. DG ECHO is recruiting one National Staff to be based in Nairobi (Kenya) as a Programme Associate (WASH, Shelter & Settlements) , for its Nairobi Regional Office. 1. Duties & Responsibilities: The jobholder carries out activities to contribute to the delivery of an effective humanitarian response in their area of expertise. The jobholder contributes to assessments, monitoring and evaluations of projects, as well as to the analysis of the humanitarian context in the area of coverage and s/he will be responsible for the following tasks, among others: Contributes to the appraisal, monitoring and evaluation of projects, including financial assessment of proposals. Critically studies and comments upon partners’ reports and field operations and reports to line manager. Assists the HoO/ТА (Technical Assistant) in the preparation of fiche-ops (e-documents completed by DG ECHO staff for assessing and monitoring projects), as appropriate. Assists with, participates in, and reports on meetings, as appropriate. Advises on the operational capacity of implementing partners. Drafts reports on the humanitarian situation, including any political, economic and security events relevant to the analysis of the humanitarian situation in the country/region. Produces and circulates information of common interest (humanitarian situation reports, background information, etc.). Accompany the TA on field visits as requested and may act as an interpreter if necessary. Assists the HoO/TA in the event of an emergency response. Prepare maps, when appropriate. Provides backstopping and surge support capacity in case of need. Undertakes any additional reasonable tasks as assigned by the TA, HoO) and/or Headquarters. Working with partners: Maintains contact with DG ECHO’s partners, advising the TA of any major issues arising. Acts as a point of contact between the activities of the Thematic Unit responsible at HQ and the partners involved in these programmes. Works closely with other employees to coordinate the activities of the responsible thematic unit at HQ in the field, including other ECHO staff from other units. Represents DG ECHO in relations to all partners. Contributes to improving partner relations by maintaining professional, user-oriented communication. Listens to partners' requests and provides support and solutions. Maintains contracts/grants database. Coordination: Participate in meetings, as requested and appropriate. Liaises with local authorities and institutions, in coordination with the HoO/TA, as delegated and appropriate. Helps to increase the visibility and communication of DG ECHO’s overall assistance. A detailed Terms of Reference (including competencies required and more detailed information on the tasks) is available at: https://echo.gestmax.eu and below TOR PA WASH Nairobi.pdf 2. Required Qualifications: Education: A relevant first level university degree, preferably in water engineering or a corresponding scientific discipline related to technical water and sanitation, or equivalent professional experience. Knowledge and experience: Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in WASH, Shelter & Settlements at national or international level in supporting programme/ project operations, including at least 2 years of experience with an NGO, UN, donor, or national/international organisation. Good knowledge of the EU humanitarian aid system. Good knowledge of International NGOs in the field of humanitarian aid/development, UN Aid Agencies and Red Cross Movement. Good understanding of Humanitarian Aid principles, policies and standards. Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, MS Excel, etc). Languages: 3. Required Competencies: Working and communicating effectively with people: ability to communicate, support and work effectively with colleagues and teams to achieve collective goals. Building and maintaining excellent relationships with colleagues and partners. Achieving impactful results and quality: ability and commitment to organise and perform the job to the highest standards, delivering consistent results and striving for quality assurance. Understanding of the humanitarian and DG ECHO way of working: ability to support DG ECHO's mandate, strategies and operations, to ensure policy compliance and in particular the correct use of the Key Results Indicators (KRIs), and to ensure DG ECHO's visibility. Ability to ensure the correct application of DG ECHO guidelines and procedures in all the decisions taken. Demonstrating exemplary attitudes and behaviours: commitment to act in line with DG ECHO and humanitarian values, demonstrating the required and exemplary attitudes necessary for the Field Network. DG ECHO applies a policy of equal opportunities. Our recruitment policy is based on respect for diversity and on maintaining the gender balance. Our human resources management provides for balance between professional and private life, and support for training and developments opportunities. For information, the employment conditions that could be proposed include an initial contract of one year with the possibility of renewal subject to a 3-month probationary period and following a positive annual evaluation. As an indication, the monthly basic salary range is KES.350,795/- (minimum corresponding to 5 years’ experience and subject to local tax law). The salary will be adapted according to the exact duration of relevant professional experience supported by a work certificate (one year of relevant experience account for one step in DG ECHO’s salary grid). In addition to this, the employee will also receive disability/retirement allowance, 13 th month salary as well as a medical coverage. DG ECHO’s employees are bound by the National Staff code of conduct which is available on the link: https://ec.europa.eu/echo/system/files/2019-09/code_of_conduct_for_national_staff.pdf Only the short-listed candidates will be contacted. Candidates who are not contacted by 30/11/2026 should consider that they have not been selected. Any form of canvassing, soliciting, or influencing will be treated as grounds for disqualification. Shortlisted candidates who are successful in the written test and who make it to the oral interview phase but are not to the final selection, could be included (depending on the results of the oral interview) in a reserve list and can be considered if a new procedure takes place for a similar post within the next 12 months. “Any processing of your personal data will be done in accordance with the applicable EU legislation (Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data.” The privacy statement can be found on DG ECHO’s website. https://ec.europa.eu/echo/system/files/2020-01/privacy_statement_recruitment_ns_final_version.pdf

item.title: EEAS Call for Expression of Interest for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) as Administrative Assistant to the Deputy Managing Director POL.EURCA.WEST.DMD - Western Europe
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The Directorate for Western Europe (POL.EURCA.WEST) works towards the comprehensive deepening of relations, and where applicable integration and accession, between the EU and our immediate neighbours in Europe, the Western Balkans, Turkey and the United Kingdom. It does so by supporting the HR/VP, the Commission, the European Parliament, the Council and Member States in their work on key aspects related to the Stabilisation and Association Processes, Enlargement, the EEA/EFTA, the special relations with Micro States, and all other institutional and legal arrangements that apply to EU relations with specific countries and regions, The Managing Directorate covers 4 Divisions and 13 EU Delegations in charge of 16 partners or partner countries. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one ASSISTANT (AST2) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. The main responsibility of the Assistant will be to provide general secretarial, administrative and logistic support to the Deputy Managing Director/Director. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Manage the agenda, e-mails (OUTLOOK CALENDAR), filtering incoming telephone calls and respond to general inquiries as needed; Set-up of appointments and manage meetings, booking meeting rooms, access requests for external visitors, assist in welcoming and accompanying visitors in accordance with EEAS security regulations; Assist the Deputy Managing Director/Director in the preparation of his/her missions and visa requests, manage his/her mission orders and costs declarations (MIPS) and requests for reimbursement of representation costs (ARES); Assist in the organisation of internal and external meetings and events and the preparation of meeting files, as needed; Monitor incoming and outgoing correspondence in ARES, ensure timely circulation of information and follow-up of deadlines, handle EU Classified lnformation (EUCl, RUE), as needed; Ensure the proper workflow of the briefings cleared by the Deputy Managing Director (e-brief); Maintain the coordination with the Managing Director's office POL.EURCA, DMD and facilitate the internal communication within the Directorate and its Divisions as well as within the EEAS and external interlocutors; Monitor leaves and absences through Sysper2 and provide logistical assistance to the line manager in dealing with the lT tools related to people management activities as needed; Ordering office supplies; This position involves regular contacts with EEAS Council and Commission Services, EU Member States permanent representations, Foreign Ministries, Embassies and external organisations. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST2. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Post-secondary education attested by a diploma followed by at least 3 years of relevant professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties OR secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 6 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: The successful candidate should have relevant experience for the job; sound computer skills; good understanding of the rules and procedures of the European institutions; good organisational and communication skills; good sense of initiative and team spirit; be flexible and service minded. Furthermore very good command of English, knowledge of French and other EU languages; experience with EEAS lT tools; and prior experience in working as an Administrative Assistant to a Director/DMD/MD; would be considered as assets. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox pol-eurca-west-dmd@eeas.europa.eu copying AST-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: " EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST2- POL.EURCA.WEST.DMD-job nr 523101" Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 23/09/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST2- POL.EURCA.WEST.DMD-job nr 523101" ) : pol-eurca-west-dmd@eeas.europa.eu 2. Pre-selection The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter. 3. Selection The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs. Depending on the outcome of future appointment procedure(s) under Article 29 of the SR for a similar profile , EEAS services may, in case no suitable candidates are found among EU officials, have other job opportunities that would involve the recruitment of the Temporary Agents under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. If any, candidates in the above-mentioned reserve list may be contacted by other EEAS services for potential recruitment. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence o

item.title: Ukraine2EU is looking for a Head of Intelligence Hub
item.description: Ukraine2EU is looking for a Head of Intelligence Hub Text Ukraine2EU is launching an Intelligence Hub — an ambitious initiative designed to consolidate and analyse public perceptions of Ukraine’s EU accession both domestically and across the EU. This Hub will support Ukrainian institutions and decision makers with evidence and analysis to inform strategic decision-making, policy, and communication. We are now looking for a strong leader to establish and guide this unit. About the role The Head of Intelligence Hub will be responsible for building and steering the Hub’s analytical and communication outputs and ensure that these are used to influence current and future policies. You will lead a team that systematically tracks public opinion, narratives, and trends, and you will ensure that insights are translated into actionable strategies for government institutions, first and foremost, but also for donors, civil society, and media. The role requires not only analytical excellence but also the ability to engage directly with policy makers and stakeholders, positioning the Hub as the first-choice knowledge partner on EU accession perceptions. You will oversee both the domestic and European dimensions of the Hub’s work — from surveys and media monitoring in Ukraine to comprehensive analytics across all 27 EU Member States. This means balancing technical oversight with strategic vision, ensuring that outputs are credible, timely, and impactful. Why this matters The Intelligence Hub is being established to equip the Ukrainian institutions leading accession with the evidence and insights needed to strengthen Ukraine’s voice and position in Europe. Leading the Hub is not just a leadership role — it is an opportunity to make a real impact. Ultimately, your work will help those carrying the responsibility for Ukraine's accession to make well-informed decisions and better understand and influence the narratives that will determine future EU membership. Requirements We are looking for a Ukrainian candidate who: Has a strong analytical mindset, and is able to engage with both quantitative and qualitative research methods. Understands the principles and importance of evidence-based and rigorous analysis and has the ability to transform complex analysis into clear, actionable insights for policy and advocacy. Has a good grasp of current debates and evidence in the area of Ukraine’s EU accession including public perceptions and how these interact with domestic and international politics. Possesses the personality, authority, and confidence to set direction and inspire a diverse team. Is adept at engaging with ministries, embassies, donors, civil society, and media, and can navigate sensitive discussions with clarity and conviction. Brings experience in managing complex, high-profile and/or analytical initiatives with multiple stakeholders, ideally in an international or EU-related context. Is fluent in Ukrainian and English. Has at least a master degree in a relevant field such as sociology, international relations, political science, international law, strategic communication, or comparable. Is proficient in MS Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, as well as other modern digital tools for data analysis and visualisation, media and social media monitoring, and the preparation of analytical materials. Location Kyiv, Ukraine (hybrid working arrangements may be available). What we offer Contract type | Service contract for 12 months with extension possibility until the end of the Programme. How to apply Please send your CV and a short cover letter (maximum 2 pages) outlining your suitability for the role no later than 25 September 2026 . Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply for this job: https://apply.workable.com/ukraine-2-eu/j/4A183D861C/apply/

item.title: Social Secretary to the Head of Delegation Section -2 Year Contract Subject to Renewal
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the United States of America, Washington DC, is looking for: Social Secretary (Local Agent Group III – Secretary) to the Head of Delegation Section - 2 Year Contract Subject to Renewal We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the United States of America in Washington, DC works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the U.S. government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Social Secretary is in the Head of Delegation section which consists of 11 people. This role works closely with other sections in the Delegation and with staff at the official Residence. The position will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Delegation, and will be assigned the following main tasks and duties: Preparation, management and execution of all official and social events hosted by the Head of Delegation (HOD) and by the Deputy Head of Delegation (DHOD); Managing all verbal and written communications with social event guests, including US and EU high-level visitors, ensuring internal communication on events within the Delegation, and developing/maintaining contacts with external parties (US Government offices/agencies, think tanks, non-profit organizations, universities, other Embassies, etc.); Reviewing invitations received and consulting with other Delegation sections as necessary to make recommendations regarding appropriate course of action; Developing and maintaining a register of contacts as well as a filing system for past events and engagements; Advising the Delegation leadership and acting as the Delegation’s point of contact on all aspects of diplomatic social protocol, US social customs and airport protocol for eligible high-level visitors; coordination with other sections on port courtesies; Main contact point for EU Member States for HOMS meetings and events with HOD (including updating/circulating EU Heads of Mission contact list) and EU HOMs’ Spouses programs and activities; Supervising the Residence staff and working with Administration on issues related to the maintenance and administration of the HOD Residence (including vendor contracts and payments). The post involves regular atypical working hours including evenings, and sometimes weekends, where there are events. We offer a competitive position in an international environment working in close coordination with colleagues across the EU Delegation. There is a competitive benefits package as follows: The basic salary range (excluding overtime) is not negotiable but determined by proof of relevant and verified employment experience, starting from $67K (1 years’ experience), $72K (4 years’ experience), $77K (7 years’ experience) etc. 24 personal leave days per year 13 to 14 Public Holidays Flexible working hours Health, dental and vision insurance Short term disability insurance Generous employer 401k contribution This is a 2 Year Contract subject to renewal. There may be 2 renewals up to a maximum 7 years of successive fixed-term contracts. An indefinite contract may be offered after 7 years. The anticipated start date is 1 November 2026. Eligibility requirements Minimum of High School/Secondary school diploma or equivalent; higher education an advantage; Minimum of 1 year’s experience relevant to the tasks of the job. We look for Excellent organization and coordination skills, detailed orientated and ability to multi-task and prioritize; Demonstrated communication skills, excellent social and interpersonal skills, discretion on sensitive matters; Ability to multi-task and prioritize in a fast-moving environment, as well as to balance demands and manage needs of multiple stakeholders Professional, proactive and persistent as well as punctual, discreet and able to safeguard confidential matters discussed by others during performance of duties; Knowledge and understanding of the Washington DC international, philanthropic and events community, the U.S. Government and political system, and familiarity with think tanks, NGOs, and cultural, educational and charitable organizations; Working knowledge of US protocol, including Order of Precedence is an advantage; Excellent spoken and written command of the English language, knowledge of other European languages would be an advantage; Excellent computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook, knowledge of scheduling tools and internet applications, as well as database experience; Experience in an international organization, a diplomatic mission, a multicultural environment or familiarity with the European Union would be an asset. How to apply It is important to note that the Delegation of the European Union does not sponsor visas for Local Agents. Applicants must have a valid US work authorization at the time of application that does not require Delegation of the European Union sponsorship. The applicant must send the following: A cover/motivation letter. Indicate in your cover letter which type of US work authorisation you have (US citizenship, Green card, EAD). Curriculum Vitae preferably using the Europass template available at: https://europa.eu/europass/en . Other CV formats will be accepted. The resume must also include the names and contact details of at least two referees who can attest to your professional and personal attributes in the event you are shortlisted for the post. References will only be taken up for those who are shortlisted. Please state in the subject of your email: Reference 03/26 – Social Secretary – [YOUR SURNAME]. Send your complete application to eeasjobs-047@eeas.europa.eu by no later than Wednesday 16 September 2026 (EST). The process After the deadline for applications, the applications will be reviewed by a Selection Panel set up for this purpose. The Selection Panel will prepare a short-list of candidates who are considered the most suitable for the post based on a preliminary assessment of the information provided in the cover letter and resume. The short-listed candidates will be invited to an assessment phase, which will include an interview and practical test. During this phase, the Selection Panel will assess the suitability of the candidates for the post. Those candidates who have not been short-listed will not be contacted individually; however, the Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this job advertisement to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The successful candidate will be subject to a background check. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. Please address any queries concerning this procedure to delegation-usa-vacancies@eeas.europa.eu . The deadline for applications is Wednesday 16 September 2026. Pay: $67,000.00 - $77,000.00 per year Benefits: 401(k) 401(k) matching Dental insurance Flexible schedule Health insurance Paid time off Vision insurance Work Location: In person

Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Administration Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in the secretarial/receptionist field. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: · Greet visitors professionally upon arrival and represent the Delegation as the first point of contact for outside visitors · Switchboard operation, placing and answering telephone calls as required · Drafting notes, letters on protocol matters, visa issues, registration of Delegation’s expatriate staff and their family members · Make sure the reception is never left unattended during office hours; organize rotation schedule with secretaries · Open, register and filter incoming mail, route mail to appropriate individuals and keep mailing lists up to date, using ARES application · Receiving and registering tenders · Addressing envelopes for local post / diplomatic pouch / driver · Filing, archiving; making paper copies and assistance in distribution of documents to staff as required · Occasional translation/interpretation and other logistical support to the organization of meetings/events/missions; · Other secretarial assistance as designated by the Head of Administration · Check ID cards and hand out visitor badges · Keep the reception room, inside and outside lobby tidy to assure a professional and representative environment for the arrival and departure of visitors. · Cooperate with the security staff present in the outside lobby · Contact relevant staff members upon arrival of visitors · Regular updating of Delegation Directory and Private Phone Numbers · Carry out Meeting rooms planning for all entities The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 11,014 SAR gross. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 15 November 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) · Upper secondary education · At least five years of experience as Administrative / Secretarial tasks · Working knowledge (C2) of English, local Arabic language · Right to residence and work in Saudi Arabia, depending on local law · Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned · Microsoft office programs, preferable ARES document management Assets / selection criteria · skills of time management, and interpersonal skills; capacity of organizing meetings · high level of computer skills (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.); · high level of language skills (written, oral) in required languages; · team work fluency, flexibility, and capacity to work under pressure; How to apply Please submit your application, consisting of a cover letter and Europass format CV ( https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv ) via the mailbox eeasjobs-142@eeas.europa.eu (Reference Secretary) no later than 10 October 2026 10.00 am. Only complete applications received on time via eeasjobs-142@eeas.europa.eu will be considered. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. 3 best candidates will be invited to the final interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this job advertisement to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality and to preventing discrimination on any grounds. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential.

item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is looking for a Policy Officer Job title: Policy Officer (m/f/x) LOCAL AGENT GROUP I Ref: 505089 – Political, Press and Information Section Who We Are? The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs among others through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sultanate of Oman and the Kingdom of Bahrain in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The EU Delegation to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. What We Offer The post of Policy Officer, Group I in the Delegation’s Political, Press and Information section, under a fixed-term employment contract of 2 years, with a possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availabilities, and operational considerations. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of 8 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed tasks depending on the needs of the EU Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the EU Delegation’s Head of Political, Press and Information Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in the field of communications, press and online presence. The following main tasks and duties are currently required: Assist the Delegation in conducting information, communication and media activities to improve the visibility of and knowledge about the EU in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sultanate of Oman, and Kingdom of Bahrain, including speechwriting. Contribute to the drafting and implementation of the Delegation's social media strategy. Assist in drafting and disseminating proactive messaging aligned with the Delegation’s and EEAS Headquarters’ communication strategies. Analyze the trends and developments in the information environment in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sultanate of Oman, and Kingdom of Bahrain, including emerging narratives and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). Provide recommendations for improving the understanding of the EU and its policies based on using fact-based information and proactive communication. Design, implement, and coordinate campaigns, local outreach events, and communications projects on specific issues and priorities, including media information relations towards the EU and its partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sultanate of Oman and Kingdom of Bahrain. Perform other tasks as designated by Head of Delegation and the Head of the Political Press and Information Section and the Head of the Delegation; co-operate closely with the other Press and Information Officer. Provide occasional support and act as a backup for the Press and Information Officer. Contribute to political reporting. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 20,473 SAR monthly. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 01 January 2027. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) University degree in a field relevant to the position (political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or related field. Minimum 5 years of professional experience in a relevant field (media, online publishing, public relations, communication, events or similar). Professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Excellent knowledge of Arabic and English. Right to reside and work in Saudi Arabia. Good standing as citizen/resident. Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Postgraduate degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or related field. Experience in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in a multi-cultural international setting. Experience working with European Union policies and procedures. Knowledge of the European Union. Experience of working in political analysis and communication including: Experience in social media communication, including drafting social media content and overseeing an online community of the EU Delegation’s social media platforms, including: Drafting social media posts Experience of working with social media analytics. Experience in public speaking. Contributing to small-scale social media campaigns. Knowledge of graphic and audio-visual tools. How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter , signed a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers’ names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en Send all documents to the following email address: Eeasjobs-151@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “ Ref: 505089 – JOB TITLE: Policy Officer “ no later than 11:00 AM (UTC+3) 31/10/2026. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based on assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing and interviews. The 3 best candidates will be invited to interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check, background check, etc.Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality, preventing discrimination on any grounds and ensuring a zero-tolerance approach to any form of harassment. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations. item.description: Job vacancy: Administrative Assistant in the Administration Section. Local agent group II Ref: 520144 – administration section We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organisations. The EU is represented throughout the world in more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the United Kingdom works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the United Kingdom government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The Delegation of the European Union to the United Kingdom opened its doors on 1 st February 2020 following Brexit and is located in central London. It is a multi-cultural environment and it currently has around 50 staff members, working across five sections: Head of Delegation Section, Political Section, Press & Information Section, two EU Policies Sections and an Administration Section. The Administration Section currently consists of 11 staff members. We offer The post of Administrative Assistant to the Administration Section is a fixed-term employment contract for two years, with the possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availabilities and operational considerations. item.title: Funded traineeships for young graduates at the EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna - Multiple sections
item.description: We offer: Traineeships of up to 6 months in 2026 within the following sections of the EU Delegation, subject to availability of the budget . The tentative start date is 1 st semester 2027 (earliest start date March 2027, possibly also 2 nd semester 2027). Traineeship in the UN section (UN): The UN section assists the Head of Delegation in his functions as Ambassador of the EU towards Vienna-based International Organisations. The section covers a dense multilateral agenda at the UNODC, UNIDO, UNOOSA and UNCITRAL inter alia, on drugs and crime, outer space, and industrial development. It prepares and coordinates EU statements and represents the EU at various UN meetings, conducts outreach to international organisations and third countries, and reports to the European External Action Service (EEAS) and the European Commission. The UN section is actively engaged in public diplomacy activities showcasing the benefits of EU-funded projects to third countries and International Organisations. Main tasks: Assisting permanent staff in the preparation of meetings and other diplomatic activities. Assisting in the drafting of briefings, reports, statements and other documents. Participating and note-taking in meetings. Assisting in public diplomacy activities. Traineeship in the OSCE Section (OSCE): The OSCE Section assists the Deputy Head of Delegation in her function as the EU Ambassador to OSCE and covers the Organisation’s agenda across its three dimensions of security: politico-military, economic and environmental, and human rights and fundamental freedoms. OSCE agenda currently focuses on Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and also addresses a wide range of topics, sun as transnational threats trafficking in human beings, economic and environmental aspects related to security, as well as human rights and fundamental freedoms. The Section represents the EU in OSCE meetings and events, prepares and coordinates EU statements and messages for numerous meetings, engages with third countries, and prepares reports/briefings for the EEAS and EU institutions. It also conducts public diplomacy to highlight EU achievements. Main tasks: Monitor developments across the three OSCE dimensions of security: politico-military, economic and environmental, and human dimension and attending OSCE meetings together with permanent staff; Assist permanent staff in the coverage of a large variety of regional and thematic dossiers. Assist permanent staff in the preparation and conduct of EU coordination and outreach activities. Assist permanent staff in drafting and reviewing EU statements and messages. Take notes and prepare reports on OSCE and EU meetings and consultations. Engage in background research on EU and OSCE related topics. Conduct background research on EU and OSCE related topics. Assist in the organization of public diplomacy activities. Traineeship in the Nuclear and Non-Proliferation section (NNP): The Nuclear and Non- Proliferation (NNP) section covers a dense multilateral agenda on security policy, focusing on nuclear and non-proliferation issues. This includes all activities of the IAEA, be it Ukraine, Iran, DPRK, Syria, or nuclear safety, security, safeguards, as well as technical cooperation. The section also covers meetings related to the CTBTO and export controls and also coordinates on the EU’s contribution to the NPT. The daily tasks of the section include chairing of EU coordination meetings, conducting outreach to international organisations and third countries, drafting EU statements, representing the EU in international fora, and preparing internal briefing notes as well as reports for the European External Action Service (EEAS) and the European Commission. The NNP section is also actively engaged in public diplomacy efforts displaying tangible results of EU action in support of the rules-based multilateral system. Main tasks: Assisting permanent staff in the preparation of meetings and other diplomatic activities. Assisting in the drafting of briefings, reports, statements and other documents. Participating and note taking in meetings. Assisting in public diplomacy activities. Traineeship in the Administrative section (ADMIN)/Head of Delegation Section (HoD): The Administrative (ADMIN) section handles essential behind-the-scenes processes to ensure the smooth daily running of the Delegation and its sections. Its responsibilities include financial and budget management, procurement, document archiving, and liaising with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on protocol matters such as VAT exemptions and diplomatic cards. The Head of Delegation section (HoD) provides strategic support to the Ambassador in heading the overall work of the diplomatic mission. It ensures internal and policy coordination across all sections, manages high-level diplomatic visits and meetings, assists in the organisation of formal and social events at the mission and the residence, oversees official correspondence on behalf of the Head of Delegation, and ensures daily agenda management. The Head or Delegation section (HoD) also handles the Delegation’s press relations, public and cultural diplomacy, and digital communications to promote the visibility of EU policies and values in Vienna. It manages the Delegation's website and social media channels, organises public events and campaigns alongside Team Europe partners, and handles the section's administrative and financial tasks. Main tasks: Assisting with general administrative / office tasks; Assisting with protocol tasks; Updating of internal guides, contact lists, distribution lists, etc.; Assisting with and / or coordinating logistical elements of meetings / visits / representation / social events; Assist in creating Social Media posts/updating Delegation website Assisting with payment files. Assisting with archiving. Filling in for ad-hoc requests. We look for: Qualifications or special requirements : A master's degree in a relevant discipline, e.g. International Politics, European Studies, International Relations, International Law, International Economics, etc. Candidates without a master's degree are NOT eligible to apply for these traineeships. A demonstrated interest in the EU's external action and in international relations, with a particular focus on security, human rights, and in the UN framework Experience in the drafting of policy documents, note taking and drafting of meeting reports Excellent English language skills Experience working for a related International Organisation or a diplomatic Mission in that context and ability to work in other OSCE languages, as well as the ability to work in other UN languages would be assets. No previous experience of more than six weeks in the EU Institutions Candidates must have less than one year of professional experience after their graduation by the signing of the Traineeship agreement. For the ADMIN section only: A bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline will suffice B2 German language skills No experience in drafting of policy documents required Numeracy essential How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address Delegation-Vienna-Trainees@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents: A detailed standard Europass curriculum vitae ( CV ) https://europa.eu/europass/en (CVs in other format will not be considered) a cover letter describing why you want to participate in a EU traineeship and an application form Please mention in the subject of your e-mail : Funded Traineeship – Your Name/Acronym of the Section - emails without this subject line will not be considered (you may only apply to 1 traineeship per delegation, however based on your profile, the delegation could offer you a traineeship in another section). Important information to read before applying Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. This information may be updated before the start of the Traineeship, in which case the candidates proposed for selection before the update will be informed. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Citizens from EU Member states: must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation; must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation.
