item.title: Funded traineeship for young graduates at the EU Delegation to Argentina
item.description: The deadline for submitting applications is 10/10/2026. Are you a young graduate interested in international relations? Are you curious to learn more about work of a diplomatic mission and how the EU Delegation represents EU interests and values in Argentina? We offer: A traineeship of 6 months in 2026 within the Politics, Press and Information Section of the EU Delegation, subject to availability of the budget . The tentative start date is November 2026. The Political, Press and Information Section monitors political, economic and social developments in Argentina, as well as relevant regional and international issues. It contributes to analysis of Argentina’s domestic politics, foreign policy and relations with the EU, and supports the Delegation’s strategic communication, public diplomacy, media and social media activities. Main tasks : As part of a team of 5 people, the intern will contribute to the following tasks: Political and analytical reports and briefings Strategic communication, public diplomacy and social media activities Media monitoring, analysis and preparation of media reviews Participation in meetings, events and conferences, including note-taking and reporting Preparation of background information Supporting the organization of public diplomacy and press events aimed at increasing the visibility of the EU in Argentina. Monitoring the Argentine daily press and preparing reports on issues of interest to the Delegation and Headquarters. Conducting research on legislation, statistics and political developments to support the preparation of reports and other documents. Compiling information on relevant EU legislation and policies of interest to Argentina for dissemination. We look for: Qualifications or special requirements : Young graduate with a university degree in Political Science, International Relations, European Studies, Journalism, Communications, Law or other relevant Social Sciences. Traineeship or other practical experience in a workplace, NGO or association ideally abroad (not exceeding 12 months). Fluency in English and Spanish (C2 level), written and oral communications; both languages used as working languages Interest in EU–Argentina relations, international affairs, political developments and strategic communication would be an advantage Experience with (professional/institutional) social media publications AI-generated applications are discouraged. How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address delegation-argentina-recruitment@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents: Please mention in the subject of your e-mail : Funded Traineeship - Pasantía subvencionada – Sección Política, Prensa e Información Important information to read before applying Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Citizens from EU Member states: must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation; must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation.

The project is implemented by Statistics Finland, French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (Insee), Italian National Institute of Statistics (Istat), Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BHAS), Institute for Statistics of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FIS) and Institute for Statistics of Republika Srpska (RSIS). Position: full-time Resident Twinning Adviser’s Language Assistant (RTA-LA) Duration : up to 18 months Starting Date for Employment (Indicative): October 2026 Place of Employment: Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina Gross monthly salary: up to 2000,00 EUR depending on qualifications NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS Compulsory requirements: Successfully accomplished higher education. Native speaker of one of the official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Ability to accurately interpret and translate to/from English/national languages (both simultaneous translation as well as written documents), with professional experience within an international office, preferably in the public administration sector. Strong drafting, report-writing and analytical skills in English, acquired through academic studies and/or professional experience. Advanced computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. Ability to meet deadlines and perform effectively under pressure, with flexibility and a commitment to achieving results as part of an international team. Sound judgement and a proactive problem-solving approach, with the ability to work independently or under limited supervision. Willingness and ability to travel within the country and internationally. Commitment to maintaining high ethical standards and acting in a non-discriminatory manner at all times. Respecting, actively supporting and, where appropriate, contributing to the overall goals and objectives of the Project. Complying with Project policies relating to conduct, appearance, health and safety, security, remuneration arrangements and the use of Project equipment. Maintaining strict confidentiality with regard to all Project-related matters. Optional requirements: RTA-LA - TASKS Supporting the RTA and other project experts in their activities as Project translator and interpreter. Providing translation and interpretation in the preparation and implementation of activities, such as training, meetings, workshops, seminars or other circumstances as required. Providing translation and interpretation assistance in the preparation of studies, documents and other material. Reviewing, translating and editing text relevant to the project (newsletters, press releases, PowerPoint presentations and documents) in English and national language(s). Accompanying the RTA or other project experts to meetings, workshops, seminars as well as to missions and field visits throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina and EU (for activities outside Sarajevo only travel and accommodation costs will be reimbursed). Providing general support for RTA and/or other experts with BC partners and/or authorities, with particular reference to missions and mission reports. Assisting the RTA in communications, liaison and general working relations with BC public offices and institutions. Performing temporarily RTA assistant duties on demand. SELECTION PROCEDURES AND DEADLINE FOR THE SUBMISSION OF THE APPLICATION How to apply CV (Europass format), cover/motivation letter in the English language and copy of the Passport will be sent to the following e-mail addresses with subject “ BiHTwinning-RTA-LA ”. bihtwinning@stat.fi For any further information please contact the above email with subject “ BiHTwinning-RTA-LA-Further Info ” Deadline 9 October 2026 - Time: 18:00 CET Should the CVs arrive beyond the above-mentioned deadline, they will be not taken into consideration. Only shortlisted candidates will be informed and invited to an interview, which will be held physically in Sarajevo (October 2026). ADDITIONAL JOB INFORMATION He/she will be contracted by Statistics Finland. Applicants shall not have been involved in the selection process nor in the drafting of the Contract Applicants may not have or recently (past 6 months) have had any contractual relation with the beneficiary administration(s). The RTA-LA will sign a full-time service contract and must have a status of self-employed. It will be his/her sole responsibility to comply with all legal requirements for self-employment as well as to cover all related taxes and charges. item.title: Vacancy Notice: In the field of Facility Management
item.description: The post (Local Agent Group II) in the Delegation’s Administration Section is part of a team consisting of 16 people. The European Union Delegation to China are seeking a highly skilled and experienced officer in the field of Facility Management to oversee the efficient operation and maintenance of our facilities. Under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Administration, the ideal candidate will be responsible for ensuring the functionality, safety, and overall well-being of our physical spaces, including office and residential buildings. The successful applicant will play a key role in optimizing operational processes, managing resources, and creating a conducive work environment for employees. The position is offered under a fixed term contract of three and a half (3.5) years, renewable once. Main tasks and duties: 1. Facility Maintenance: Develop and implement a comprehensive maintenance program to ensure the proper functioning of all facilities. Coordinate and supervise maintenance activities, including repairs, renovations, and upgrades. Conduct regular inspections to identify and address potential issues proactively. Support strategic planning related to the Delegation’s long-term infrastructure needs, including scenario analysis and investment planning. 2. Space Planning and Utilization: Optimize the layout and utilization of space to meet organizational needs and accommodate growth. Plan and execute space reconfigurations and furniture allocation needs as required. Ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations in all space planning activities. 3. Vendor Management: Source, negotiate with, procure (e.g. needs definition, market surveys, tendering), and manage relationships with external service providers and vendors. Oversee contracted services, such as cleaning, security, and landscaping, to ensure high standards are maintained. Evaluate vendor performance and initiate improvements as needed. 4. Budget Oversight: Develop and manage the facility budget, ensuring cost-effective operations. Monitor expenses, analyse variances, and implement cost-saving measures without compromising safety and quality. 5. Health and Safety Compliance: 6. Environmental Sustainability: 7. Emergency Response and Business Continuity: 8. Infrastructure Planning and Capital Projects Lead and coordinate the identification, assessment, and selection of new premises in line with operational, technical, and security requirements. Manage building-related projects, including new construction, refurbishment, and fit-out works, from initial planning through to completion and handover. Act as the focal point for external stakeholders, including architects, engineers, contractors, and interior designers, ensuring effective coordination and delivery of projects. Oversee project governance, including timelines, budgets, procurement processes, and quality control, ensuring compliance with applicable rules and standards. Translate operational needs into technical specifications and functional layouts, ensuring optimal space planning and workplace design. Monitor project risks and propose mitigation measures to ensure timely and cost-effective delivery. The base salary will depend on pertinent and verified employment experience, typically starting from CNY 24,317. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days, health insurances, and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be December 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Bachelor's degree in Facility Management, Engineering (civil, mechanical, electrical), Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field, degrees in Project Management or Real Estate/Property Management can also be considered where combined with relevant professional experience. Minimum 3 years proven experience in Facility Management, Engineering (civil, mechanical, electrical), Architecture, Construction Management. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Mandarin. Right to residence and work in China. Pass the required pre-recruitment medical exam. Assets / selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Strong knowledge of facility management principles, health and safety regulations, and environmental sustainability practices. Excellent organizational and planning skills. Exceptional communication and interpersonal abilities. Proficient in using facility management software and tools. Knowledge of CAD software (e.g. AutoCAD) is an advantage. If you are a strategic thinker with a hands-on approach to facility management and possess the ability to create and maintain a safe, efficient, and pleasant working environment, we invite you to apply for this exciting opportunity. The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Beijing , China works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the other EU Member States missions. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Chinese government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. How to apply The application should include a cover letter and a detailed CV in English, using the Europass CV format: https://europa.eu/europass/en/create-europass-cv . Please email your application to eeasjobs-109@eeas.europa.eu Please mention: Family Name – First Name – ADMIN Section, in the subject line. The deadline for reception of the applications is set for 17hrs on 26 October 2026 (GMT +8) . The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure by telephone. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee; please address any queries concerning this procedure to the above-mentioned mailbox with a reference: Question – ADMIN SECTION . The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing, and interviews. The highest qualified candidates will be invited to the final interview and/or practical test planned during July/August 2026. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check-up and background check. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this job advertisement to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The European Union Delegation is an equal opportunity employer, who believes that diversity is good for our people and our business. Therefore, we promote the inclusion of suitable, qualified, and experienced staff and welcome different characteristics with regard, for example, to their gender, age, racial or ethnic origin, religion or beliefs, sexual orientation/identity, or disability. Personal data are processed in the context of recruitment in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of 23 October 2018 on the protection of natural persons regarding the processing of personal data by the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The section consists of 6 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Political, Press and Information Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in all communication, social media and press activities. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 16/11/2026. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES SOCIAL MEDIA & DIGITAL COMMUNICATION Prepare and disseminate press releases, press reviews, and articles for media and internet publication, ensuring that messages are consistent with the Delegation’s key communication priorities Prepare communication materials such as speeches, briefings, and information for the media, drawing, where appropriate, on strategic storytelling approaches used in the Delegation’s communication campaigns Monitor local and European media and prepare press reports, including elements useful for assessing public diplomacy efforts and communication campaigns Maintain and develop relationships with local and international journalists, media organisations and government press agencies Manage media requests and coordinate responses with the relevant internal stakeholders, in order to ensure coherent and timely communication Organise press coverage during official missions and events, including, where relevant, coordination with communication service providers involved in campaigns or visibility activities EVENT MANAGEMENT & PUBLIC OUTREACH Lead the preparation of public diplomacy events, public outreach activities, high-level visits, and site visits for the Ambassador and other EU officials, in support of the Delegation’s strategic communication and visibility objectives Coordinate with cultural, academic, and diplomatic partners to enhance event impact and ensure successful public diplomacy campaigns, contributing to maximising the visibility and perception of the European Union Coordinate local outreach activities and organise cultural and visibility events to promote EU values and activities, ensuring, where relevant, coherence with ongoing communication campaigns STRATEGIC SUPPORT & ADMINISTRATION Support in drafting reports, strategic documents, and preparing internal and external communication plans, including contributions related to communication campaigns and visibility activities Provide input for Terms of Reference and support the practical steps of procurement and contract management for communication service providers (e.g. preparing draft specifications, following up on deliverables), under the guidance of the management and in line with the applicable rules and procedures. Assist with the planning and management of the Delegation's press and information budget Collaborate with EEAS Headquarters' services and strategic communication task forces to ensure consistent messaging and alignment of communication strategies, acting, where appropriate, as a contact point for exchanges on communication activities at Delegation level The duties and responsibilities may be adapted according to the evolving needs of the European Union and its diplomatic representations. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) 5 years of relevant professional experience (media, online publishing, public relations, communication, events, etc.) University degree (Bachelor or equivalent level; ISCED level 6) Excellent command of written and oral Arabic (CEFR C2 level) Excellent command of written and oral English (min. CEFR C1 level) Right to residence and work in the country Medical fitness to carry out the required duties Certificate of good conduct Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Experience working in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in an international organisation Experience working with the European Union tools, policies and procedures Experience working with external contractors for communication or visibility activities University degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or similar (bachelor’s degree or equivalent; ISCED level 6) University degree in political science, communication, international relations, media, journalism, public relations or similar (master’s degree or equivalent; ISCED level 7) Language certification in Arabic (CEFR C2 level) and English (min. CEFR C1 level) Knowledge of other languages (depending on country requirements) Language certification in other languages (depending on country requirements) How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter, signed a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers’ names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en all documents to the following email address: Eeasjobs-140@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “Ref: 523802 – JOB TITLE: Press and Information Officer” no later than 18:00 14 October 2026, Damascus time . Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates-based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing and interviews. At least the 5 best candidates will be invited to the final interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The same means of publication used for this job advertisement will be used to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed whether a candidate has been recruited. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check and a background check. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response. item.title: Team Leader in the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4)
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. Part of the Directorate for Policy Planning and Strategic Communication (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT), the main task of the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4) is to defend the EU’s values and interests by understanding and effectively addressing Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), including through data monitoring and analysis. The division develops strategies and policy approaches to counter FIMI and advance information integrity, leading the implementation of related policy instruments such as the FIMI toolbox and manages dedicated cooperation structures, including the Rapid Alert System. It contributes to the detection and analysis of FIMI, informing evidence-based countermeasures to FIMI, with a specific focus on FIMI threat actors most relevant to the security of the EU and our partners. It undertakes a number of activities to bolster information integrity and resilience inside and outside the EU, including awareness raising, training, and other forms of public engagement offline and online such as the EUvsDisinfo project. Furthermore, it works closely with the global network of EU Delegations and the EU’s CSDP missions and operations, while building partnerships with key international partners, such as NATO or the G7, and civil society organisations. WE LOOK FOR We are looking for a highly motivated, dynamic, flexible and proactive colleague, with proven expertise in the field of countering FIMI. The successful candidate will be based in the Data Knowledge and Analysis Team in the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4 Division and will operate horizontally across the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4 Division, coordinating tasks with other EEAS teams, other EU institutions, Member States, international partners and in close interaction with the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT management. WE PROPOSE The post of a Team Leader position to lead the FIMI Data Knowledge and Analysis Team Leader in the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4). The Team Leader is responsible for : Designing, coordinating and implementing a strategic and operational approach that transforms analytical outputs and data-driven insights into active operational and impactful responses to counter FIMI in coordination with other teams. Coordinating the activities of the EEAS FIMI Situational Awareness Hub, which aims to turn data into high quality analysis and effective responses, ensuring the effective planning, reporting, and administrative coordination of the team's work. The role will contribute to the EEAS's strategic communication efforts and oversee the technical implementation of the FIMI Deterrence Playbook. The standardisation of FIMI detection and analysis and developing and implementing FIMI methodological capabilities (FIMI Exposure Matrix, TTPs analysis, FIMI Deterrence Playbook, OSINT capabilities…), taxonomies and data-sharing standards (STIX), and technical tools (DataScienceLab, AI capabilities, leverage OpenCTI databases…). The position will drive the enhancement of interoperability between internal and external systems, promote the automation of analytical and operational processes, and ensure that FIMI threat analysis is translated into coherent, scalable, and impact-oriented operational responses in support of the organisation's objectives. This position also involves preparing briefings and documentation, capacity-building activities, supporting inter-service coordination, ensuring compliance with internal procedures, monitoring the implementation of work plans and deliverables and overseeing budget planning and contracts management. Key responsibilities will include: Coordinate the implementation and maintenance of FIMI analytical methodologies, taxonomies, data models and interoperability standards (e.g. Information Manipulation Set, TTPs categorisation, STIX…). Oversee the development and integration of technical capabilities supporting FIMI detection and analysis, including OSINT methodologies, AI-enabled capabilities, and technical tools, such as DataScienceLab and OpenCTI. Guide and lead FIMI-related threat analysis capabilities and investigations. Ensure FIMI data integration, information exchange and interoperability across internal and external stakeholders. Coordinate the preparation of technical documentation, reporting and briefings. Coordinate the data-driven implementation of the FIMI Deterrence Playbook linking FIMI Threat analysis to concrete response actions across policy, disruption, law enforcement, sanctions and strategic communication. Monitor the implementation of technical work plans, analytical deliverables, and response operational processes ensuring compliance with established procedures. Assess effectiveness through data-driven evaluation to support EEAS actions and communication. Support administrative and financial management activities, including budget planning and implementation, procurement procedures and contract management, in accordance with applicable financial and administrative rules. Conduct capacity-building activities, presentations, and representing the Division on relevant matters This position is classified as an “Administrator” type of post 1 in the grade bracket AD 5 – AD 12. As temporary agents under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (hereafter, the “CEOS”), the duration of the assignment to the post shall, in principle, be four years dependent on the maximum duration of engagement in the EEAS allowed by their type of contract 2. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: Immediately LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The successful candidate for this position will be appointed in accordance with Article 29(1)(a) and Article 98(1), second subparagraph, of the Staff Regulations (SR) and Article 2(b) of the CEOS. WE LOOK FOR Eligibility criteria 3 : In addition to the conditions set out in Article 12 of the CEOS, candidates must: Have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and/or additional language); possess a level of education: which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma when the normal period of university education is four years or more, OR which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma and relevant professional experience of at least one year when the normal period of university education is at least three years. have at least 5 years full time professional experience. This experience must have been gained after obtaining the four-year diploma or after obtaining the three-year diploma and the one-year relevant professional experience. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents and are ineligible. Selection criteria: Candidates should have: an excellent ability to maintain diplomatic relations and to ensure representation, communication and management in a complex, multicultural environment; an excellent capacity to create constructive working relations with national authorities, civil society, international organisations and EU Member States; strong drafting, communication and analytical skills combined with sound judgement; excellent knowledge of the EU's internal and external policies and instruments, and of the functioning of the Union and its inter-institutional framework; experience and knowledge of CFSP and CSDP; possess technical, operational and strategic expertise on countering FIMI threats; have strong expertise in OSINT methodologies, evidence collection, latest tools and AI-solutions for detecting, analysing, investigating, and reporting FIMI threats; have a strong knowledge and understanding of analytical frameworks and data sharing standards, such as STIX; experience in assessing information environment, hybrid and FIMI threats, to characterise threat actors’ capabilities and TTPs; proven ability to design innovative initiatives in the countering FIMI field, including data-driven projects on technical disruption and law enforcement; demonstrate flexibility and resilience in managing high workloads and operational priorities, with the ability to perform effectively under significant pressure, including outside normal working hours; have experience in preparing and delivering

item.title: Команда підтримки відновлення та реформ Міністерства Енергетики України шукає Експерта/ку з Інвестиційної підтримки енергосистеми
item.description: Команда підтримки відновлення та реформ Міністерства Енергетики України шукає кваліфікованого фахівця чи фахівчиню на посаду: З детальним описом вакансії (ToR) можна ознайомитись за посиланням вище. Команда підтримки відновлення та реформ допомагає Міністерству Енергетики у впровадженні пріоритетних реформ. Команда підтримки відновлення та реформ є частиною програми «Архітектура відновлення та реформ в Україні» (URA), запровадженої Європейським банком реконструкції та розвитку (ЄБРР) у партнерстві з Європейським Союзом для підтримки важливих процесів відновлення та реформ в Україні. Кінцевий термін подання заявок: 23:59 (за Київським часом), 8 жовтня 2026 року. Потенційні кандидати мають подати: ● заповнену аплікаційну форму ; ● угоду про нерозголошення ; ● резюме кандидата; ● контактні дані трьох рекомендодавців, які зможуть підтвердити професійний досвід та/або освіту кандидата. Завантажити аплікаційну форму та угоду про нерозголошення можна за посиланнями вище. Документи необхідно надіслати на електронну пошту rst.mev@gmail.com у зазначені вище строки. Усі документи мають бути підготовлені англійською мовою. Кандидати, які подали неповний пакет документів, не розглядатимуться як претенденти на посаду. URA реалізується за підтримки Багатостороннього донорського фонду стабілізації та сталого розвитку України ЄБРР за фінансової участі Австрії, Данії, Фінляндії, Франції, Німеччини, Італії, Японії, Латвії, Нідерландів, Норвегії, Польщі, Словенії, Швеції, Швейцарії, Великої Британії, США та Європейського Союзу.

item.title: EUBAM Rafah - Vacancy Announcement – Various positions (4 posts)
item.description: The European Union Border Assistance Mission for the Rafah Crossing Point – code name EUBAM Rafah – was launched on 24 November 2005 to monitor the operations of the border crossing point between the Gaza Strip and Egypt, after Israel and the Palestinian Authority concluded an Agreement on Movement and Access on 15 November 2005. The Council of the European Union approved that the EU should undertake the third-party role proposed. EUBAM Rafah is currently seeking dynamic, highly skilled candidates for immediate recruitment to fill the following Four (4) vacancies: SECL 01 Mission Security Assistant (1 post): main responsibilities are related to providing security and operational support to Mission staff, monitoring the security situation, and supporting security procedures, risk assessments and travel arrangements. HRL 02 Human Resources Officer (1 post): main responsibilities are related to recruitment, staff administration, training, HR records and systems, and supporting payroll and other HR-related processes. HRL 03 Human Resources Assistant/Travel (1 post): main responsibilities are related to coordinating official travel and entitlements, maintaining HR and travel records, and providing administrative support to the HR Office. HoML 02 Protocol/Administrative Officer (1 post): main responsibilities are related to protocol, liaison and administrative support to the Head of Mission and Deputy Head of Mission, including official visits, events and coordination with external stakeholders. Employment regime: Locally Contracted Staff hired under Israeli Local Labor Law Duty Station: Ramat Gan - Tel Aviv Opening Date: 01 October 2026 Closing Date: 23 October 2026 General employment/eligibility requirements: Education and professional experience, as well as proficiency in English, Arabic and Hebrew, as specified in the relevant Job Description; a valid identification document permitting employment and unrestricted movement within the Mission’s area of operations; medical fitness for work; and a clean criminal record. IMPORTANT: Work is expected to be performed physically at the Mission offices in Ramat Gan, Monday through Friday. Candidates must be able to make the necessary arrangements to travel to and from the office premises on a daily basis. Applicants must hold a valid local identification document or work permit authorising employment at the Mission. IMPORTANT INFORMATION FOR THE APPLICANTS Applicants are reminded that the work of the Selection Committee is strictly confidential. Therefore, applicants must not contact, either directly or indirectly, any member of the Selection Committee, nor request that any other person do so on their behalf. item.title: EEAS Call for Expression of Interest for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) as Desk Assistant (AST3) in POL.MENA.2
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The MENA2 Division is responsible for EU policy towards Isarel, the occupied Palestinian territory and the Middle East Peace Process. It coordinates internally, including with Member States and with relevant Commission services and agencies; interacts with civil society and the European Parliament; and leads on institutional engagement with Israel and the Palestinian Authority. To note that the Division encounters an increasingly heavy workload in a politically sensitive geographical area, demanding tasks of various nature, pressing deadlines for a relatively small team, where everyone needs to perform optimally, show high resilience and work as a team player. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one ASSISTANT (AST3) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Monitoring and analyzing developments in Israel, the occupied Palestinian territory and the Middle East Peace Process, as well as related developments in the MENA region and the international arena; Contributing to the definition, implementation and communication of relevant EU policies in close coordination with Commission services and Member States; Drafting and contributing to briefings, statements, information for the general public, lines to take for the press, reports and other documents; Ensuring effective coordination and liaison with other EEAS Divisions, EU Delegations and Offices, Commission services, the Council and the European Parliament; Assisting in the preparation of internal and external meetings and high-level visits As required, take on any additional tasks related to the work of the Division. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Post-secondary education attested by a diploma followed by at least 3 years of relevant professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties OR secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 6 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: experience in the field of external relations and on the Middle East region; good understanding of the external relations, internal policies, and rules and procedures of the EU institutions; experience and knowledge of CFSP and CSDP; strong drafting and analytical skills combined with sound judgement; a good sense of initiative and team spirit, and the capacity to perform with accuracy and in a flexible manner a diversity of tasks in a complex institutional environment; Furthermore would be considered as asset. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox POL-MENA-2@eeas.europa.eu copying AST-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: " EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST3-POL.MENA.2-job 171032 " Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 21/10/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b- AST3-POL.MENA.2-job 171032 " ) : POL-MENA-2@eeas.europa.eu 2. Pre-selection The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter. 3. Selection The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs. Depending on the outcome of future appointment procedure(s) under Article 29 of the SR for a similar profile , EEAS services may, in case no suitable candidates are found among EU officials, have other job opportunities that would involve the recruitment of the Temporary Agents under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. If any, candidates in the above-mentioned reserve list may be contacted by other EEAS services for potential recruitment. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion . The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email

item.title: PROJECT OFFICER LOCAL AGENT GROUP I Ref: 522934- Cooperation Section
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, Amman works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Jordanian government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Project Officer (Local Agent Group I) in the Delegation’s Cooperation Section, under a fixed-term employment contract of 2 years, with a possibility of renewal under reserve of budgetary availabilities and operational considerations. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of 24 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed to functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Cooperation, providing support, expertise and assistance in communication, visibility and public diplomacy activities related to the EU's cooperation portfolio in Jordan. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: Programme and Project Management Contribute to all stages of the EU project cycle, including programming, identification, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation programmes. Monitor the implementation of EU-funded projects through regular reviews, meetings, field visits and reporting. Coordinate and supervise monitoring, evaluation and communication missions. Contribute to the preparation and management of calls for proposals and procurement procedures, including evaluation processes where appropriate. Ensure compliance with contractual obligations, including communication and visibility requirements. Provide operational support and quality assurance for programme documentation and reporting. Communication, Visibility and Public Diplomacy Contribute to the design, implementation and monitoring of the Delegation's communication and visibility strategy for EU cooperation in Jordan. Develop and coordinate communication plans supporting EU-funded programmes and initiatives. Coordinate the production of communication materials, including publications, factsheets, success stories, videos, photography and digital content. Organise and oversee visibility events, campaigns, exhibitions, conferences, cultural diplomacy initiatives and public outreach activities promoting the EU-Jordan partnership. Ensure compliance with EU communication and visibility guidelines across all externally funded actions. Coordinate communication activities with implementing partners and provide guidance on visibility obligations. Build and maintain effective working relationships with Jordanian authorities, EU Member States, international organisations, civil society organisations, media representatives and other stakeholders. Media Relations and Content Development Research, draft and edit articles, speeches, press material, success stories and other communication products highlighting EU priorities and cooperation achievements. Coordinate with the Delegation's Communication Unit on media engagement and press activities. Support senior management through the preparation of speeches, talking points, presentations and briefing materials. Digital Communication and Community Engagement Coordinate communication campaigns across digital platforms. Produce and oversee the production of engaging multimedia content for the Delegation's social media channels. Support the management of online communities and monitor public engagement and audience perception. Contribute to maintaining and updating the Delegation's website and other digital communication platforms. Internal Coordination and Reporting Prepare reports, briefings and analytical notes for Headquarters and Delegation management. Coordinate communication training and awareness activities for Delegation staff and implementing partners. Ensure proper management of documentation and records using the European Commission's corporate information systems, including Ares and OPSYS. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 2919 JOD. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be mid November 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Minimum required qualification: University degree in Communication, Journalism, Public Relations, International Relations, Political Science or related field. Minimum of 5 years of professional experience, in communication, visibility, public diplomacy, project management and social media management. The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. At least three (3) years of professional experience in digital communication, digital storytelling, content development, digital advertising and web / social media metrics. Experience in event management and excellent organisational skills. Experience in managing or monitoring international development cooperation programmes. Knowledge of European Union external action, development cooperation and communication policies. Experience working with donor-funded projects, international organisations or diplomatic missions. Excellent spoken and written command of the English and Arabic language. Right to residence and work in Jordan. Good standing as citizen/resident. Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Capable of producing high quality results within often tight deadlines, motivated, ability to work alone and /or in a team, ability to deal with stress situations. Excellent communication skills, including presenting information clearly both orally, in writing and on digital platforms. Strong sense of initiative and creativity. Ability to work in team and coordinate teamwork. Ability to multi-task and priorities and flexibility with regard to working hours. Knowledge of IT tools, including tools for graphic and video content editing and digital platforms / social media management. How to apply The applicant must apply by sending all documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-193@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “ Ref: 522934 – JOB TITLE: PROJECT OFFICER IN THE COOPERATION SECTION“ no later than 16:00 (Amman local time) 21/October/2026. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. At least three best candidates will be invited to the final written test and interview. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality, preventing discrimination on any grounds and ensuring a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation (DELEGATION JORDAN VACANCY DELEGATION-JORDAN-VACANCY@eeas.europa.eu ) in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations DATA PROTECTION NOTICE: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/eeas-privacy-statement-data-protection-notice-purpose-processing-persona

National Authorities nominating candidates are kindly requested to send the respective application forms using the Annex 2 and cover letter to the following email address: EUROPE-2@eeas.europa.eu or delegation-bosnia-and-herzegovina-eusr-personnel@eeas.europa.eu For contracted candidates: Interested candidates who wish to apply for vacancies open to contracted candidates, should use the standard application form (Annex 2) and submit the application together with the cover letter to the email address below: delegation-bosnia-and-herzegovina-eusr-personnel@eeas.europa.eu General aspects for seconded candidates: Interested candidates should use the standard application form (Annex 2), in which they can list all positions for which they are interested. It is essential that both the job title and corresponding reference number are clearly marked in the form. Information: For more information related to the selection and recruitment, please contact: Dalila Basic (Ms) – EUSR in Bosnia and Herzegovina Tel: + 387 33 560 837 email: delegation-bosnia-and-herzegovina-eusr-personnel@eeas.europa.eu For updates on this position and other EUSR positions please check our website https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/bosnia-and-herzegovina_en APPLICATION FORM ANNEX 2 - APPLICATION FORM - EU Special Representative in BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA Seconded Personnel – For seconded positions, only personnel nominations received through official channels from EU Member States will be considered. Contributing States will bear all personnel-related costs for seconded personnel, including salaries, medical coverage and travel expenses to and from the Mission area (including home leave). Contracted Personnel – The EUSR may recruit international staff on a contractual basis as required, through an employment contract. The employment contract with the EUSR establishes the conditions of employment, rights and obligations, remuneration, allowances, travel and removal expenses and the applicable standard risk insurance policy. Documents supporting educational qualifications and work experience, if issued in another language, should be accompanied by certified translations of the original documents in English language in accordance with the article VI.1.2 of the Guidelines on the main principles of classification of posts and grading of international contracted staff. The EEAS, Western Balkans Division, requests EU Member States and European Institutions to second experts or to support the applications for contract regime to the available position with the EUSR in BiH, according to the described requirements and profile: GENERAL CONDITIONS Citizenship – Citizen of a Member State of the European Union (EU) and enjoying full rights as a citizen. Integrity – The candidates must maintain the highest standards of personal integrity, impartiality and self-discipline within the EUSR Team. Candidates are not allowed to provide or discuss any information or document as a result of access to classified and/or sensitive information related to the EUSR Team or respective tasks and activities. The candidates shall carry out their duties and act in the interest of the EUSR. Flexibility and adaptability – The candidates must be able to work in arduous conditions with a limited network of support and with unpredictable working hours and a considerable workload. They must have the ability to work professionally as a member of the team with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and must be able to cope with possible extended separation from family and usual environment. Physical and mental health – The candidates must be physically fit and in good health without any physical or mental problems or substance dependency which can impair operational performance. Serious deficiencies in any of these general conditions may result in repatriation/termination of the secondment/contract. REQUIREMENTS II.A Essential Requirements The following are essential requirements in respect of international experts to the EUSR in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the Job Description: Education and Training The candidates should have a recognized academic qualification under the European Qualifications Framework (EFQ), or equivalent, at a level specified in the individual job descriptions. Knowledge The candidates should have good knowledge of the EU Institutions and international standards, particularly related to the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP). Skills and abilities Language Skills – The candidates must be fully fluent in written and oral English language. Communication and Interpersonal Skills - The candidates must have excellent interpersonal and communications skills, both written and oral. Organizational skills - The candidates must have excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritise work to meet tight deadlines, and a concern for order and accuracy. Computer Skills – Skills in word processing, spreadsheet and e-mail systems are essential. Knowledge of other IT tools will be an asset. Driving Skills – Be in possession of a valid, including Bosnia and Herzegovina, civilian driver licence for motor vehicles (Category B or equivalent). Being able to drive any 4x4 wheel drive vehicles. Serious deficiencies in any of these essential requirements may result in repatriation/termination of the secondment/contract. II.B Desirable Requirements Knowledge of the Western Balkans – The candidates should have good knowledge of the history, culture, social and political situation of the Western Balkans, in particular through field experience in a multilateral working environment. Language - Proficiency in local language(s) will be considered an advantage. ESSENTIAL DOCUMENTS AND REQUIREMENTS FOR THE SELECTED CANDIDATES Passport – The selected candidate must obtain a passport from their respective national authorities. Possession of a valid diplomatic or service passport for seconded participants is optional. Visas – Contributing States and selected candidate must ensure that visas are obtained for entry into Bosnia and Herzegovina prior to departure from their home country. It is also essential to obtain any transit visas, which may be required for passage through countries en route to the Western Balkans/Bosnia and Herzegovina area. Education diploma(s)/certificates or/and professional certificate(s) - The selected international candidates must have and present to the Mission the University diploma or the professional certificate/diploma, depending on the job description, before signing the contract or the taking up duties. Personnel Security Clearance (PSC) –The selected candidate will have to be in possession of Personnel Security Clearance (PSC) at least “EU Secret” level. The seconded experts, the original national security clearance or a proof of initiation of the process must accompany them upon deployment. For contracted experts, if necessary, the process may be initiated by EUSR BiH. Medical Certificate – The selected candidates should undergo a medical examination and be certified medically fit for mission duty by a competent authority from the member State. This certification must accompany deployed seconded/contracted personnel. Deficiencies in any of the documents asked for a specific position may result in failure of the selection process. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE SELECTION PROCESS Gender balance – The EU strives for improved gender balance in CSDP operations in compliance with UNSCR 1325. The EUSR in Bosnia and Herzegovina encourages Member States and European Institutions to take this into account when offering contributions. Application Form – Applications will be considered only when using the standard Application Form (Annex 2) and indicating which position(s) the candidate is applying for. Application form must be accompanied by a cover letter . Selection process - The candidates considered to be most suitable will be shortlisted and interviewed by audio/video skype/phone, before the final selection is made. Information on the Outcome – Candidates applying for the contracted positions as well as Member States and European Institutions will be informed about the outcome of the selection process after its completion. Data Protection – The EUSR Office processes personal data pursuant to Regulation (EC) 2018/1725 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the EU institutions and bodies and on the free movement of such data, as implemented in the EEAS by the Decision of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 8 December 2011. The Privacy statement is available on the EEAS website. Job Description – The current reporting lines of the following job descriptions might be subject to modification based on the operational requirements. item.title: Secretary in the Political, Press and Information Section

Register in Ares where appropriate and dispatch accordingly; follow-up and make appointments as instructed by the Head of Section Act as a pro-active first point of contact for the Delegation's PPI Section and advise the Section accordingly. Check, maintain overview and process correspondence to the Head of Section and the Section in line with instructions Manage the PPI Section's electronic filing and maintain the PPI Section's contact databases and mailing lists. Take minutes of PPI's meetings. Act as the PPI's Section's procurement contact Under the guidance of the Head of Section, draft a weekly media review of key issues and events in the Delegation's area of responsibility Assist with the upkeep of the Delegation's dedicated website, social media sites, including Twitter, Facebook and Instagram As appropriate, assist with event management and organisation for Delegation outreach events, including Europe Day reception and European Film Festival; maintain an overview on the planning of events and deadlines When needed, accompany members of the Delegation to media/ promotion events, to assist with photography, report writing and general support Coordinate annual leave and mission planning of the Head of Section and other staff members within the assigned Section as instructed by the Head of Section The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 251000 JMD. item.title: VACANCY NOTICE: PRESS AND INFORMATION ASSISTANT
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Ukraine in Kyiv works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Ukrainian government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of a Press and Information Assistant (Local Agent Job Profile of Press and Information Assistant, Group II) in the Delegation’s Political, Press and Information Section. The team consists of 15 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Press and Information Team, providing support, expertise and assistance for communication tasks and activities and secretarial support to the Head of P&I and the Press and Information team. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: SECRETARIAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT Provide day-to-day administrative and organisational support to the Head of Press and Information and the Team, including: Organising meetings, public events, high-level visits and missions from Brussels, including logistical coordination with Ukrainian authorities and other counterparts. Managing calendars and supporting regular coordination meetings with EU Member States and other stakeholders. Supporting media relations and communication with local and international media. Providing translation and interpretation support as required. Collecting and consolidating information for regular and ad hoc reporting. Managing incoming calls, emails and correspondence and liaising with Ukrainian ministries and other official counterparts. Drafting and processing correspondence, including letters, cover notes, registration and distribution. Maintaining filing and archiving systems and supporting internal administrative workflows. Performing other tasks assigned by the Head of Team. PROJECT MANAGEMENT Coordinate and support the implementation of Press and Information projects. Assist with the operational and financial management of projects and related activities. Support other projects as required. MEDIA Assist the Head of P&I in managing media relations, media communities, engagements and interviews. Monitor media and relevant EU-related news as required. Support the preparation and implementation of media projects, including seminars, press trips and other media events. Assist with press conferences and media activities related to high-level visits. WEBSITE AND SOCIAL MEDIA Manage and regularly update the Delegation’s website, ensuring key information and materials are easily accessible. Prepare, coordinate, translate, schedule and publish content for the Delegation’s social media channels (X/Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Support the development of social media content and communication products. COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION ACTIVITIES Distribute EU publications, promotional materials and other communication products to the public, EU Information Centres, libraries and relevant networks across Ukraine. Manage the Delegation’s news and information subscriptions, including assessment of needs, subscription arrangements and monitoring. Receive, process, archive and distribute electronic news from Ukrainian information agencies to relevant recipients. Handle external information requests and coordinate responses. PROCUREMENT, FINANCE AND CONTRACTS Support and manage P&I procurement processes, particularly for digital and communication-related projects. Draft tender specifications and prepare procurement dossiers, including invitations, technical specifications, contracts and purchase orders. Register contractors and relevant procurement documentation. Prepare budget estimates and commitments and monitor expenditure under P&I contracts. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 3 207 USD currency. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be December 2026 . Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) University education with at least bachelor’s degree; Minimum of two years of experience in the area of communication, financial management, contracting or similar. The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Knowledge: Good understanding of communication related issues; Good understanding of the Ukrainian and world media landscapes; Good understanding of management institutional or organisational social media accounts; Good secretariat and organisational skills; Good drafting skills in both Ukrainian and English; Understanding of procurement, project management and coordination issues; Working knowledge (C2) of English (Listening, Reading, Spoken interaction, Spoken production, Writing); Working knowledge (C2) of Ukrainian (Listening, Reading, Spoken interaction, Spoken production, Writing); Knowledge of IT tools: Strong computer skills and knowledge of IT tools; Right to residence and work in Ukraine; Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Knowledge of EU external action and public diplomacy; Knowledge of French; Knowledge of digital solutions streamlining internal work; Familiarity with social media analytics tools (e.g., Meta Business Suite, Twitter Analytics, Hootsuite, Sprout Social); Basic photo/video editing skills (e.g., Canva, Adobe Express, CapCut, Premiere Rush). Personal skills Motivated and enthusiastic team-player, able to efficiently prioritise tasks and respect deadlines; good communication skills; flexibility and dedication; strong self-organisation skills. How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter in English, signed a Curriculum Vitæ in English (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en all documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-049@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “Ref: 521658 – JOB TITLE: PRESS AND INFORMATION ASSISTANT“ no later than 22/10/2026. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. item.title: Trainee - EUSR for the Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue based in Brussels
item.description: We offer: A traineeship of 6 months within the office of the EU Special Representative for the Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue. The EU Special Representative for the Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue is mandated to achieve comprehensive normalisation of the relations between Serbia and Kosovo, enhance the Union visibility and effectiveness through public diplomacy and contribute to the unity, consistency and effectiveness of Union action. The trainee will be fully embedded in the work of the EUSR’s office, receive direct exposure to its activities in the Western Balkans and in Brussels, and have the unique opportunity to understand the work of an EUSR from the inside. Main tasks: Provide active input to the EUSR’s work. Assist the work of the EUSR’s team as necessary. Support monitoring, analysing and reporting; conducting research and drafting briefings. Contribute to administrative tasks as required. Take part in meetings and ensure timely and quality reporting. When needed draft notes/briefings/background information as requested. Contribute to and take part in the organization of meetings and events. Assist in the organisation of missions of the EUSR and incoming visits. Contribute to outreach, communication, and public diplomacy activities. We look for: Qualifications or special requirements: Bachelor degree in international relations, political science, European studies, law, economics, communication or a related field and completed or ongoing master studies. Nationals of a Member State of the European Union. Excellent drafting skills in English. Ability to handle politically sensitive issues in a responsible manner. Proven interest for EU affairs and neighbourhood policies. Experience in research and analysis. Computer literate with practical experience in Microsoft packages. Good networking, interpersonal skills and attention to details. Experience in working in a team and in coordinating inputs from various colleagues. How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address EUSR-DWB@eeas.europa.eu and send the application form with the following subject: “ FirstName LastName – Traineeship-EUSR-Dialogue ”. Only application forms sent in electronic PDF format (not scanned) will be considered. Important information to read before applying Applicants who have already benefited or currently benefit from any kind of training or employment within a European Union institution, body, agency or office are not eligible. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. The trainee will receive a monthly grant of 1,572.00 € according internal and Belgium employment regulation. This amount is subjected to Belgium social security taxation. All costs related to travel, insurance, accommodation, and living expenses must be borne by the trainee. The trainee will be responsible for costs arising from accidents and/or illness incurred during the traineeship and must show proof of a valid medical insurance coverage, including that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidate is not able to present the required documents, their candidacy will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Annexes:
